proposed.demonstrated_gap: FastMCP has two gaps against mcporter on the bridge verb. (1) Trace context across the bridge. The 2026-07-28 revision carries W3C traceparent/tracestate in _meta (SEP-414). Claude Code exports TRACEPARENT to Bash-tool subprocesses when OTel tracing is enabled. For mcporter, 'traceparent' was not found in GitHub code search of openclaw/mcporter, and its CHANGELOG at v0.14.2 has no trace-context entry. A traced agent-to-bridge-to-server call therefore loses its parent at the bridge. FastMCP documents client-side spans (`tools/call ... (CLIENT)`) and trace-context propagation on outbound requests in _meta. Its telemetry docs say native mode propagates, and propagation_only mode states that 'Outbound requests still carry traceparent and tracestate in _meta'. For the `fastmcp call` CLI, injection needs an OTel SDK, and pickup of an inherited TRACEPARENT is unverified; that is the trial's first measurement. (2) The bridge head-to-head on record (receipts 6 and 12, 2026-09-23) has a single third-party arm, wong2/mcp-cli 2.0.0, which is now stale (0 default-branch commits since 2026-07-08). Since 3.0.0, FastMCP has shipped an MCP client CLI covering the same verbs: `fastmcp list` (tools, resources and prompts; --input-schema/--output-schema; --json; --auth oauth|bearer|none), `fastmcp call` (schema-driven coercion, --json) and `fastmcp discover --source claude-code`. FastMCP 4.0.0 is built on the 2026-07-28 revision and Python SDK v2, and negotiates the best mutual protocol era by default (#4572). All 8 GitHub advisories against it are fixed in 3.2.0 or earlier, so none affects 4.0.11. The CLI page read states no Horizon (paid hosting) requirement; v4.0.0 adds a Horizon auth client (#4785). This is a lighter local arm for the same trace-context trial as today's agentgateway targeted proposal, so the two can run together.

Use the 8 call and 5 list operations of receipts 6 and 12, plus one 2026-07-28 stateless fixture server, three runs each. Measure the pass rate; tool-name and schema equality against Inspector tools/list; cold and warm median latency (mcporter's keep-alive daemon against fastmcp's per-command runs); and the negotiated revision per server. Then run under opentelemetry-instrument with TRACEPARENT exported, as Claude Code's Bash tool does. For each arm, record whether a fixture server that logs _meta receives a traceparent carrying the caller's trace-id. The same harness can host the agentgateway arm. Decision rule: FastMCP joins as the complement for traced calls if it passes every parity check and delivers the caller's trace while mcporter does not. It replaces mcporter only if it also matches mcporter's warm latency. Otherwise it drops to keep_but_compare.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: MXC is the vendor-official counterpart of the winner's engine. GitHub Docs say GitHub Copilot CLI's local sandboxing is powered by MXC, just as Claude Code builds its sandbox on @anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime, but the layer has never compared the two head to head. MXC documents three things that srt 0.0.77/0.0.78 does not. (a) One versioned JSON policy runs over OS-native backends (bubblewrap on Linux, Seatbelt on macOS) and, on Linux only, escalates to lxc and to experimental microvm (Nanvix) and hyperlight VM backends. That addresses open gap 4 (no VM-boundary qualification) without changing the policy format. (b) The bubblewrap backend installs a default-DROP egress chain in a private netns: IPv6 egress is denied outright, DNS is not opened, and ingress and hostLoopback are denied explicitly. These target gap-0 classes (IPv6, DNS) that the srt receipts do not establish. (c) v0.9.0 adds 'Stop descendants outliving teardown' cleanup. Weak points to measure rather than assume: there is no built-in hostname allowlist (MXC sends no host lists, so domain policy needs a separately configured external proxy). Copilot docs describe the macOS proxy as env-var cooperative. No resource limit beyond timeoutMs was found in the README or the bubblewrap and lxc docs. LXC filtering requires root. Every release is a prerelease (v0.9.0, 2026-09-29). The bubblewrap proxy and firewall modes need slirp4netns, which is absent on the WSL2 host.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: On linux-wsl2-x86_64, run the layer's gap-wave2-20260923 fixtures under srt 0.0.78 and under MXC v0.9.0 lxc-exec (bubblewrap backend, schema 0.9.0-alpha, egress default deny, the same upstream filtering proxy supplied through runtimeConfig.networkProxy). The fixtures are the network extension (IPv4 loopback HTTP, TLS, SOCKS, DNS rebinding, IPv6, remote hosts), the versioned filesystem fixture, overlapping denyRead/write and the socat readiness race. Repeat with Seatbelt on macos-arm64. Record per-fixture escapes, first-request failure rate, leftover mounts and processes after SIGKILL, and p50 start latency. MXC replaces or joins the winner only if it blocks at least one fixture class that srt lets through (for example IPv6 or raw-socket egress) with no filesystem-fixture regression. Otherwise srt stays and MXC is recorded as the Copilot-side engine.
evidence: https://github.com/microsoft/mxc/blob/1ad92022d22e/README.md: 'sandboxed code execution system for running untrusted code (model output, plugins, tools) on Windows, Linux, and macOS'. Backends include Bubblewrap, LXC, Seatbelt, MicroVM (NanVix) and Hyperlight. The Linux default is bubblewrap, with lxc, microvm and hyperlight as alternatives; macOS has seatbelt only. microvm and hyperlight are experimental. 'On non-Windows platforms, all telemetry functions are no-ops'.

https://github.com/microsoft/mxc/blob/1ad92022d22e/docs/bwrap-support/bubblewrap-backend.md: deny-by-default filesystem (WSL /mnt/wsl/resolv.conf bound). A default-DROP egress chain runs in the private netns, 'DNS is deliberately not opened', 'IPv6 egress is denied outright'. egress rules take IPs and CIDRs only, and hostname policy belongs to an external proxy. The bubblewrap backend has no state-aware lifecycle.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: The layer's next_action asks for one OCI/VM candidate to compare with srt on filesystem, network and resource enforcement, state cleanup and host compatibility, and open gap 4 records no resource-limit or VM-boundary qualification. Quicksand is Microsoft's rootless, Docker-free QEMU VM sandbox for AI agents (created 2026-04-14; quick-sandbox v0.12.0 on 2026-09-14), and one API covers both hosts. accel=auto selects KVM on Linux (the WSL2 host exposes /dev/kvm) and HVF on macOS, both rated near-native. A bundled QEMU comes from the pip extras, and the WSL2 host has no system QEMU. It provides a separate guest kernel and no shared filesystem unless one is mounted. Networking is isolated by default: MOUNTS_ONLY is SLIRP restrict=on, which blocks all guest outbound traffic, and NONE is -nic none. Guest memory, cpus and disk_size are limited per sandbox, and per-sandbox qcow2 overlays support checkpoint/revert and save/load for state cleanup. srt offers none of the resource or VM-boundary properties. Limits to measure: networking is coarse (FULL is unrestricted, with no domain allowlist). QEMU is a larger attack surface than Firecracker or libkrun. The TCG fallback is 10-50x slower. Its 55 stars are no evidence either way.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: Run the same untrusted-workload fixture on both hosts under quicksand (NetworkMode.NONE and MOUNTS_ONLY, memory=2G, cpus=2, one read-write mount) and srt 0.0.78. The fixture covers (a) the network set, including IPv6, DNS, TLS, SOCKS and remote hosts; (b) reads and writes outside the mount; (c) hostile resource workloads (fork bomb, an 8 GiB allocation, disk fill) while measuring host RSS, CPU and responsiveness; (d) leftovers after normal exit, SIGKILL of the host process and checkpoint revert; (e) cold-start and exec latency on WSL2 KVM and on the M5 Pro with HVF. Adopt quicksand as the layer's VM tier if it contains every hostile workload with no host impact and no leftovers on both hosts at acceptable latency. Reject it if nested KVM under WSL2 forces TCG or mounts fail.
evidence: https://github.com/microsoft/quicksand/blob/298ba69fad80/README.md: 'async Python API to launch, control, and snapshot QEMU virtual machines with a particular focus on sandboxing AI agents'. It 'supports x86_64 and ARM64 across macOS, Linux, and Windows' and 'needs no root privileges or Docker'. Options include memory, cpus, disk_size, network_mode NONE/MOUNTS_ONLY/FULL, mounts and save, plus checkpoint and revert.

https://github.com/microsoft/quicksand/blob/298ba69fad80/docs/user-guide/07-network-and-isolation.md: the stated security boundary is a separate kernel, no shared filesystem by default, no network by default and no root on the host.

https://github.com/microsoft/quicksand/blob/298ba69fad80/docs/under-the-hood/07-network-and-isolation.md: 'restrict=on blocks all outbound connections from the guest to the real network', while hostfwd and guestfwd tunnels are unaffected. NONE is -nic none, and forwards bind to 127.0.0.1.

https://github.com/microsoft/quicksand/blob/298ba69fad80/docs/under-the-hood/02-sandbox-lifecycle.md: accel=auto selects HVF on macOS, KVM on Linux and WHPX on Windows, rated 'Near-native'. The TCG fallback is '10-50x slower'. Each sandbox gets its own overlay.qcow2.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: The separate-edits winner, worktrunk, has never been compared with what the installed clients ship. The installed Claude Code 2.1.292 has native worktree isolation: -w/--worktree [name] and --tmux, subagent and agent-definition isolation: worktree, the EnterWorktree and ExitWorktree tools, WorktreeCreate and WorktreeRemove hooks, worktree.baseRef and worktree.sparsePaths, and automatic stale-worktree cleanup that never falls back to rm -rf. Unlike a worktree manager, it also enforces write scope. Worktree-isolated sessions refuse Bash commands that cannot be shown to stay inside the worktree, and background sessions cannot edit the shared checkout until they enter a worktree. The installed codex-cli 0.160.1 has --worktree ('Run the session in a new managed Git worktree'). The same repository holds Anthropic's reference dev container: Dockerfile, devcontainer.json and init-firewall.sh, which limits outbound traffic to allowed destinations. That container is the vendor's OCI tier for unattended runs. The native Bash sandbox is the winner itself and is not a separate candidate. worktrunk keeps cross-client merge, squash and CI features that the native flags lack, and that is what the comparison must weigh.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: Run the same 3-agent parallel edit task on this repository in three arms: worktrunk v0.80.0 (wt switch -c, wt merge, wt remove), Claude-native (claude -w <name> plus one subagent with isolation: worktree) and Codex-native (codex --worktree). Measure writes that land outside the assigned worktree, including deliberate escape attempts through cd and redirects. Also measure worktrees, branches and locks left after normal exit, a crash and SIGKILL, the operator steps and wall time to merge back to main, and hook parity. Retire worktrunk to an optional merge helper if the native arms show zero leakage and zero leftovers with no more steps. Keep it as the winner if its merge and cleanup path wins or cross-client parity requires it.
evidence: Installed help for Claude Code 2.1.292 (claude --help, 2026-10-06): '-w, --worktree [name] Create a new git worktree for this session (optionally specify a name)' and '--tmux Create a tmux session for the worktree (requires --worktree)'.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: The layer lists E2B (the e2b-dev/E2B SDK) as a conditional alternative because its boundary is a hosted service. Its runtime repository, renamed from e2b-dev/infra, now documents E2B Embed: 'the whole stack, real Firecracker sandboxes included, on a single Linux host with KVM' via docker compose. That gives a self-hosted microVM boundary with resource controls on the WSL2 host, which has /dev/kvm and docker, without the hosted service. Limits: upstream calls Embed 'an evaluation package, not a production deployment pattern'. It runs on Linux with KVM only, so the Macs have no path. proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: On the WSL2 host, compare E2B Embed at release 2026.30 with quicksand on sandbox create and resume latency, egress control under the network fixture set, enforced memory and CPU limits under the hostile workload, host leftovers after kill and after pause/resume, and the control plane's idle footprint. Promote it to targeted only if it beats quicksand on containment or latency by more than the cost of the control plane and the missing macOS path.

claude_discover.notes:
Winner health. No winner is archived, renamed or relicensed. anthropics/sandbox-runtime v0.0.78 (2026-09-30; pin 0.0.77) changed tests, documentation, Linux zsh exit status, a deny-path race (#618) and CI trusted publishing. The v0.0.78 notes and the first 2,500 characters of the v0.0.77 notes show no resource-limit feature and no socat readiness fix. The DNS-rebinding-adjacent fix 'Refuse allow-listed hostnames that resolve to loopback, link-local or configured private ranges' (#522) shipped in v0.0.76, so the 0.0.77 pin already has it. Anthropic's docs call the runtime 'a beta research preview' and say that on Linux/WSL2 it builds the deny list once at launch, so it does not cover repositories created later by git init or git clone (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandbox-environments). The Claude Code CHANGELOG has 0 entries pairing sandbox with memory, cpu, cgroup or resource, so open gap 4 stands. max-sixty/worktrunk v0.80.0 (2026-09-27) has a breaking change (commit hooks now run on a detached HEAD during a squash) and adds a sigstore-signed packslip. The installed wt is v0.80.0, ahead of the recorded pin 0.79.0. Its license is NOASSERTION (information only).

Incumbency. Both winners rest on incumbency for the comparisons that matter. sandbox-runtime has never been compared with MXC, the other vendor's engine of the same class, and macos-arm64 is untested. worktrunk has never been compared with the native client worktree surfaces (Claude Code --worktree since 2.1.49; Codex --worktree in 0.160.1). Both have only native_proven receipts on WSL2.

Seeded items. None of the 21 judged repositories is re-proposed. The only new upstream evidence found is that codex-cli 0.160.1 now lists --worktree; it bears on the worktrunk half and is folded into the anthropics/claude-code entry as the Codex arm. containers/bubblewrap is the default Linux backend of both srt and MXC and is not a separate proposal. The stale list (daytonaio/daytona, metatool-ai/metamcp, context-labs/mactop, batrachianai/toad, QuantConnect/mcp-server, duckdb/duckdb-skills) is not proposed; its staleness is taken from the seed and was not re-verified here. The vendor-official pass covered installed claude 2.1.292 and codex-cli 0.160.1 --help, a GitHub search of 15 vendor orgs, and Claude Code and GitHub docs.

Checked but not proposed:
- google/gvisor: release-20260928.0 (2026-09-30), 1,042 commits since 2026-07-08. Linux only, so the out_of_scope disposition holds for the Macs. It is the runtime that agent-sandbox delegates to.
- google/nsjail: 3.6 (2026-03-18), 67 commits since 2026-07-08. cgroup v1/v2 limits on memory, pids and CPU, plus rlimits, Kafel seccomp and pasta networking; Linux only. It is a resource-limit complement, but first compare it with the OS-native baseline: the WSL2 host already has systemd-run and cgroup2 cpu, memory and pids controllers (user delegation not checked).
- google/minijail: 9 commits since 2026-07-08, last release linux-v18 (2023-05-23). Low activity, not stale.
- hyperlight-dev/hyperlight-sandbox: v0.7.0 (2026-09-12). Wasm Python/JS guests in Hyperlight micro-VMs, with an allow_domain allowlist and default writable-output limits (5 MiB per file, 20 MiB total, 20 files). Needs KVM, MSHV or Hyper-V, so no macOS. Same interpreter class as the judged pydantic/monty, and also an experimental MXC backend.
- microsoft/agent-governance-toolkit: v4.1.0 (2026-06-09). A governance and policy layer, not an isolation runtime.
- docker/sandbox-kit-spec: pushed 2026-10-06. Part of the judged Docker Sandboxes line.
- e2b-dev/E2B: SDK e2b@2.53.1 (2026-10-06).
- Third-party leads from a web search were not opened or verified (Code Airlock and Clawk aggregator pages) and are not proposed.

Host facts (read-only, linux-wsl2-x86_64, 2026-10-06). /dev/kvm is present (root:kvm 0660; the user's kvm group membership was not checked). docker, bwrap, socat and systemd-run are present; podman, qemu-system-x86_64, slirp4netns and lxc-start are absent. cgroup2 offers cpu, memory and pids controllers.

Unverified. A secondary blog (dsebastien.net) says no MXC profile should be treated as a security boundary. That wording was not found in the MXC README; GitHub Docs instead place local sandboxing at the 'lighter-weight end'.

Critic leads for the next sweep:
- A vendor-org search keyed on 'sandbox' misses microsoft/mxc, whose description reads 'Policy-driven, layered isolation and containment' and which has no topics. Add 'isolation', 'containment' and 'execution' to the org query.
- No candidate yet offers a built-in hostname allowlist together with a VM boundary on both hosts.
- The resource-limit gap on Linux may close with OS-native systemd-run scopes before any new tool.

Skills. iterative-retrieval staged discovery from a vendor-org search to metadata, then READMEs, then backend docs. From supply-chain-risk-auditor, only its interpretive rules were applied: the rename e2b-dev/infra to e2b-dev/runtime was followed, archived status and default-branch commits were checked, and unknowns were not treated as risk. Its collector scripts were not run, because candidate manifests are not local and cloning is not allowed. search-first was not invoked, because the user's rule reserves it for the coordinator, not a delegated child. The advisor was rate-limited and gave no review.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: WSL containers (WSLc) are Microsoft's own VM-backed OCI runtime. They became generally available in 3.0.1 (2026-09-29), and wslc.exe and wslcsession.exe are already installed on the linux-wsl2 host. For the layer's NEXT step, WSLc is a VM-backed OCI arm that needs no nested KVM. Gaps against the current picks: (1) sandbox-runtime has no CPU or memory limits and no VM boundary (10-01 record, isolation slot role). (2) The OCI/VM default F4, rootless containers on the hosting engine, depends on cgroup delegation that microsoft/WSL#41492 reports broken on WSL 2.9.x. That issue is still open; it was last updated 2026-09-28. What WSLc offers: `wslc run` accepts --cpus, --memory, --network, --rm, --ulimit and --gpus (ContainerRunCommand.cpp L35-75). The SDK also documents session-level CPU-count and memory settings and two networking modes, NONE and BRIDGED. According to the architecture post, wslservice.exe creates each session's VM through HCS and hands it to a per-user wslcsession.exe, and each session has its own VHD. That implies a VM separate from the distro's utility VM but does not state it, so the trial must confirm it first. Differences from sandbox-runtime to measure: (a) WSLc has no egress allow-list (networking is only NONE or BRIDGED, while srt filters by domain through host proxies). (b) It has no pids-limit flag, only --ulimit. (c) No read-only root filesystem or capability arguments are defined in ArgumentDefinitions.h. Limits on any claim: Microsoft's security model says WSL 'is not a security sandbox for running untrusted code' and that containers in WSL inherit runtime and WSL properties. That applies equally to srt and to rootless containers in the distro, so no arm on this host counts as a boundary from the Windows host, and every claim here covers only the workload versus the distro. Using WSLc from inside the distro goes through a wrapper script: the GA post lists craigloewen-msft/wslc-remote, which this worker did not check. Not established: the installed WSL version (only file dates were seen), and CUDA on the RTX 4090 (the API has GPU-enable flags). WSLc does not apply to the macOS hosts; apple/container is the counterpart there.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: Use the 10-01 frozen suite on the WSL2 host at the WSL version the trial records, with at least 30 trials per probe per arm. Arms: srt v0.0.78; F4, a rootless container on the hosting engine; and WSLc through wslc.exe, driven from the distro. Gate 0 is that a WSLc container does not share the distro's utility VM: it has a different kernel boot ID and sees none of the distro's processes or files unless they are mounted. If it fails gate 0, WSLc becomes keep_but_compare and its gap shrinks to resource limits. Metric: the pass rate over: denied out-of-tree reads and writes; denied and allowed egress (--network none and bridged); --memory and --cpus read back from the session kernel and held under memory, CPU and process-count stress; nothing left after stop and kill (processes, containers, session VMs, VHDs under %AppData%\Local\wslc\sessions); and Claude Code and Codex running unchanged inside. WSLc replaces F4 in the OCI/VM slot if its enforcement-and-cleanup pass rate beats F4's with a 95% interval on the difference that excludes zero. This includes F4 failing to start per WSL#41492. srt stays the default for tasks that need a filesystem rule set or an egress allow-list unless WSLc matches it on those probes.

It addresses the hostile-workload part of GAP4 ('No candidate has a resource-limit, hostile-workload or VM-boundary qualification'). As shipped it cannot qualify this layer's arms. WSLc cannot run inside its nested Linux-VM design, and srt could only be added through new scenario variants written against its task structure. Its kernel scenarios need pre-built VM images (README L190). Maintenance: one commit on the default branch in the 90-day window (9fa5f26c2ef1, 2026-08-13) and no releases. It requires Python >=3.13 and either AWS EC2 credentials or a third-party Vagrant provider pulled from git (uv.lock pins jasongwartz/inspect_vagrant_sandbox@ac4ff42b13a0).

claude_discover.notes:
WINNER HEALTH. These facts come from the input's 2026-10-06 components_vs_upstream check; this worker did not re-fetch them because the GitHub API budget was spent. sandbox-runtime is pinned at 0.0.77, behind v0.0.78 (2026-09-30). worktrunk is pinned at 0.79.0, behind v0.80.0 (2026-09-27). The apple/container alternative is at 1.4.1, behind 1.5.0 (2026-09-29). None is archived or renamed.

INCUMBENCY. sandbox-runtime and worktrunk stand on native_proven evidence for their narrow roles. sandbox-runtime has no CPU or memory limits (10-01 record). The OCI/VM slot's no-install default F4, rootless containers on the hosting engine, stands by the frozen rule ('could_not_separate': true in the 10-01 record), not by an enforcement or safety finding. The 10-01 record cites the SandboxEscapeBench paper as recommending that plain Docker isolation be treated as insufficient; the paper body was not re-read in this round. microsoft/WSL#41492 is still open and reports that rootless Docker and Podman cannot start any container on WSL 2.9.x. F4's host compatibility on WSL 3.0.x is therefore unverified.

VENDOR SECURITY MODEL. microsoft/WSL doc/docs/technical-documentation/security.md says WSL is not a security sandbox for untrusted code. This applies equally to srt, to rootless containers in the distro and to WSLc. Credit no arm on the linux-wsl2 host as a boundary from the Windows host, and scope every boundary claim to the workload versus the distro.

FP-CHECK VERDICTS. (1) Claim: inspect_vagrant_sandbox supplies the missing VM arm. FALSE. The provider is the benchmark's outer containment (README L10), not an arm under test. (2) Claim: WSLc is a VM boundary separate from the distro. PLAUSIBLE, not confirmed. Renamed from rivet-dev/sandbox-agent: GraphQL repository(owner:"rivet-dev",name:"sandbox-agent") returned nameWithOwner rivet-dev/agents. It holds two projects. Sandbox Agent is a Rust server plus TypeScript SDK that controls Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Cursor, Amp or Pi over HTTP+SSE: 'streaming events, handling permissions, managing sessions', with a 'Universal Session Schema' for storage and replay, in embedded mode (local subprocesses) or server mode. Rivet Agents runs agents such as Pi as durable Rivet Actors. Neither vendor gives one event schema across both worker families. Their remote surfaces are Codex-only and experimental (exec-server, remote-control) or Anthropic-hosted (claude --cloud). It therefore touches two overturn branches: remote/container worker (held by OpenHands SDK) and durable state. Today's earlier agent-sdks sweep return listed it as a completeness lead for the durable multi-host condition. No such need is qualified yet (next_action). Maintenance: the 2026-09-29 sweep recorded it stale (0 default-branch commits since 2026-07-01, last push 2026-06-19). Drive the gap-0 frozen task for both vendors next to the native openai-codex app-server arm and the `claude -p` stream-json arm. Count event types delivered versus native, a typed interrupt with usage, resume of a stored session after the server process is killed, permission round-trips and integration code size. proposed.demonstrated_gap: Native surface of the installed client (Claude Code 2.1.292 = upstream v2.1.292, 2026-10-06), proposed under the vendor-official pass for the task-attribution requirement (catalog activation 'preserve writer/task attribution'). The repository's own runbook names the unanswered case: Claude withholds OTEL_* from subprocesses, so a worker launched through a shell is not tagged, and exact child attribution must not be inferred from logs alone (token-adoption-e2e RUNBOOK lines 97-102). The native fix is documented: with beta tracing active, Bash subprocesses inherit a W3C TRACEPARENT, and a claude -p or Agent SDK child makes its claude_code.interaction span a child of that caller span; llm_request spans carry model, effort, duration_ms, ttft_ms and token counts. The stack sets OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER=none and collector.yaml has no traces pipeline, trace_statements or connectors, while the otelcol-contrib on PATH (0.162.0) already bundles span_metrics and file, so no new component or second store is needed. Two cheaper native keys are also unused: prompt.id (links all events of one prompt) is in none of collector.yaml's six keep_keys lists at ecfa1127 (78-key log list at line 233), and OTEL_METRICS_INCLUDE_REPOSITORY (2.1.269+, default false) is unset; its vcs.* attributes would also need resource, log and metric allowlist additions, which raises a cardinality and private-repository-name question. Prior record: the 2026-09-26 sweep noted the prompt.id drop and a 'Step 0 null path' inside a trace-store candidate, and the 2026-09-29 returns judged trace stores (Jaeger, Tempo, Phoenix) with 'No requirement line or open gap names one' [a trace question]; the runbook's child-attribution case is that question, and the native surface needs no store. Since then upstream added the tool.output span event (2.1.283) and fixed tool.blocked_on_user spans (2.1.288). Privacy precondition: the stack sets OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS=1, which puts serialized tool_input on claude_code.tool spans, so a fail-closed span allowlist must exist before any traces pipeline. Whether a Codex child honors TRACEPARENT is unverified.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: Bounded WSL2 trial with two cases. Case A (child attribution): one claude -p parent task whose Bash tool launches a child claude -p with tracing enabled in the child's own command or settings; traces go to the existing loopback collector through a new transform trace_statements keep_keys allowlist, then span_metrics (latency by span name only, so token usage is not captured twice) and the file exporter. Adopt traces if the child's interaction span parents under the parent's tool span, the summed span token counts per trace equal the parent's plus the child's own result usage exactly, the logs-only null path (session.id, ecosystem.task.id, prompt.id) cannot join the child to the parent task, and an extended privacy_canary.py finds 0 canaries (one placed in tool_input) in any store while its positive control leaks without the allowlist. Case B (null path, no traces): a multi-prompt interactive session with prompt.id added to the log allowlist; adopt that key if per-prompt token totals grouped by prompt.id equal the per-turn usage in the session transcript (joined by message.uuid). Overturn traces if the logs-only path also joins the child exactly in Case A, or if span export cannot avoid a second, non-deduplicable capture of the same usage.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: Route qualification today is serving observation, not a workload benchmark: gap-wave2 receipt 8 ran the llama.cpp route at --parallel 4 and --ctx-size 8192 with outputs capped at 32 tokens and states the latencies 'are shared-host observations, not a benchmark'; the Mac evidence is llama-bench pp/tg throughput. Neither replays the request mix this layer observes. GuideLLM v0.8.0 (2026-09-30), from the vLLM project org that ships the stack's pinned vllm component, replays a content-free trace (kind trace_synthetic: timestamp, input_length, output_length, optional duration, with synthetic prompt generation) through its openai_http backend against any OpenAI-compatible route (llama-server, vLLM, the OmniRoute gateway), reports TTFT and ITL distributions with SLO-aware sweeps, and runs on Linux and macOS. The privacy-filtered Loki store already keeps the needed fields for Claude api_request events (event.timestamp, input_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cache_creation_tokens, output_tokens, duration_ms; collector.yaml line 233), so a replay file needs no new capture. Fidelity limits the trial must carry: prompt length is input_tokens + cache_read_tokens + cache_creation_tokens (input_tokens alone excludes cached tokens); most Claude Code requests exceed an 8192-token context, so a preregistered fit rule is needed; telemetry has no hash_ids, so prefix reuse is not modeled and TTFT will read pessimistic; the tool calls /v1/chat/completions while Claude Code would call /v1/messages, so it qualifies the engine, not the Anthropic adapter; content-free replay measures neither answer quality (promptfoo remains the output harness) nor speculative-decoding (DSpark/MTP) acceptance. Its otel format replays recorded gen_ai.input.messages, which transform/privacy removes, so only trace_synthetic fits. Supply chain: no known OSV advisory for guidellm 0.8.0; no OpenSSF Scorecard report; no published security policy.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: Shared head-to-head of vllm-project/guidellm and ai-dynamo/aiperf, identical in both entries: one replay file R exported from Loki (one week of Claude api_request events: timestamp, prompt length = input_tokens + cache_read_tokens + cache_creation_tokens, output_tokens), replayed unchanged by both tools at the recorded arrival rate against the pinned llama-server route on the RTX 4090 and on one M5 Mac, three runs each. Preregistered fit rule: if fewer than half of R's requests fit the route's context window, the route runs at a context that fits the median request; if no host can, the trial is unqualified. Ground truth is llama-server's per-request timings object (prompt_ms, predicted_per_token_ms) captured server-side for the same requests. A tool passes if it completes R on both hosts, its p50/p95 ITL is within 10% of the server's predicted_per_token_ms p50/p95, its p50/p95 TTFT is within 10% of the server's prompt_ms plus one predicted_per_token_ms (queueing is negligible at the recorded rate), and run-to-run variation stays under 5%. If only one tool passes, adopt it. If both pass, adopt AIPerf only if its --otel-url metrics reach Prometheus through the existing collector allowlist without new unbounded labels or a new store; otherwise adopt GuideLLM. If neither passes, keep llama-bench plus server-side metrics.

proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn:
Setup: the WSL2 RTX 4090, during a window when the production generation unit is idle or stopped. Use the pinned vLLM 0.30.0 with the embedding server co-resident, a fixed context of 8192 tokens (the production route's ctx-size, not the card's 131072), and the same reasoning parser on every vLLM arm (built-in nemotron_v3). Send the slot's deciding-comparison request shapes to every arm, with the same concurrency, reasoning and output budgets.

Arms:
- A: ibm-granite/granite-4.2-8b in BF16.
- B: ibm-granite/granite-4.2-8b-fp8.
- B2: granite-4.2-8b with online --quantization fp8_per_tensor.
- Control: the production llama.cpp Qwen3.8-27B UD-Q4_K_M route.

Measure:
- Fidelity against A: a fixed lm-evaluation-harness subset, plus a promptfoo set covering JSON-schema validity, tool selection and arguments, and multi-turn tool completion.
- Peak VRAM.
- TTFT and inter-token latency, read from vLLM's and llama.cpp's own /metrics through the existing Prometheus, so no second capture path is added.
- Privacy: no request content leaves the host.
- Recovery: restart-to-first-token after a kill. Online FP8 re-quantizes at every load; the offline artifact does not.

Decision rule, fixed before the run: B or B2 passes fidelity only with at most a 1-point absolute drop against A on the lm-eval subset and zero JSON-schema or tool-call regressions on the promptfoo set. A passing FP8 arm is adopted as the optional route or fallback only if it also beats the control's TTFT and ITL with no CPU offload and recovers within the control's restart time. Otherwise the FP8 class closes for this host.

proposed.demonstrated_gap:
This is the llm-tracing slot's provisional sole trace store, checked against this layer's winners. It is current: v3.20.1 was released 2026-10-02 (the same version is also tagged langwatch@v3.20.1 and langwatch-3.20.1), and the latest default-branch commit is d96113ba11e7 on 2026-10-06.

The winning pipeline stores no traces. The collector's service pipelines are logs, metrics, metrics/health and logs/sdk_receipts, and transform/privacy is wired only into the logs and metrics pipelines. Both client templates also set traces to none. Claude Code 2.1.292 ships beta spans behind CLAUDE_CODE_ENHANCED_TELEMETRY_BETA=1. The span names claude_code.interaction, claude_code.llm_request and claude_code.tool are present in the installed binary, and the feature is documented, but it was not executed here. LangWatch would hold that per-turn span tree.

Its own coding-agent setup (langwatch claude / langwatch instrument claude) does two things that conflict with this layer:
- It turns on four content flags: OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS, TOOL_DETAILS, TOOL_CONTENT and RAW_API_BODIES.
- It exports traces, logs and metrics straight to LangWatch.
That is a second, unfiltered capture path, and it duplicates Loki and Prometheus.

The only placement without duplicate capture keeps the collector as the clients' single OTLP endpoint. The collector would get a traces pipeline with its own span privacy statements and an otlphttp exporter to /api/otel/v1/traces, which needs a new locally generated ingest key. Logs and metrics stay in Loki and Prometheus.

'Only Node.js required' still means three data services: npx @langwatch/server provisions ClickHouse, PostgreSQL and Redis itself, and the Helm baseline is about 2.8 CPU and 6.9 Gi of requests. No required trace question that the current logs-plus-metrics path cannot answer has been shown yet, so overturn_when is not met.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn:
Run the slot's own unrun deciding comparison (LangWatch vs OpenLIT vs MLflow, with Jaeger as the generic OTLP control), but through this layer's single capture path. One real Claude Code task and one real Codex task run with traces enabled, export once to the collector, and fan out to each store traces-only over otlphttp. Measure:
(a) The privacy canary extended to span attributes: zero content keys in the store with content flags off. LangWatch's own Drop policy and [SECRET] redaction count only as a second layer.
(b) Span-tree completeness and reconciliation: tool calls, subagents, durations and token/cost attributes must match the Loki events and Prometheus counters for the same session id.
(c) A named trace question, such as a subagent's share of turn latency, that Loki and Prometheus cannot answer.
(d) Total CPU, RAM and disk across ClickHouse, Postgres, Redis and the app, against the Jaeger control.
(e) Restart persistence, and collector file_storage queue replay after a store outage.
LangWatch becomes targeted only if (c) exists and it passes (a), (b) and (e) at a cost no worse than the alternatives.

proposed.demonstrated_gap:
This repository is vLLM-org official. The input pin af206d991b51 is the 2026-10-05 default-branch head, not the 0.14.0 tag (2026-09-22).

The vendor-native baseline is the stack's own installed vLLM 0.30.0. It already quantizes BF16 to FP8 at load time (fp8_per_tensor / fp8_per_block) with no checkpoint and no calibration. Its hardware table lists llm-compressor FP8 W8A8 and Marlin (GPTQ/AWQ/FP8/FP4) as supported on Ada. IBM also publishes the Granite 8B FP8 artifact, so under never-self-write the Granite FP8 arm uses that artifact.

The remaining Ada-relevant gaps are:
(a) A hashable offline FP8 artifact for a model without a vendor FP8 checkpoint. The stack already pins file_sha256 for its GGUF, and an offline artifact avoids re-quantizing at every restart.
(b) W4A16 INT4 (GPTQ/AWQ via Marlin on Ada) for models FP8 cannot fit in 24 GB. RedHatAI already publishes Qwen3.8-27B-INT4, the family production serves today as a UD-Q4_K_M GGUF on llama.cpp with --n-cpu-ffn 20 partial CPU offload.
(c) Calibrated FP8 KV-cache scales, if the online FP8 arm fails on fidelity.

Every one of these needs a vLLM generation route, and llama.cpp is the optional route today. That is the critic's own fit caveat, so no gap is demonstrated now. NVFP4 and MXFP4 compute (the README's lead news) is not native on the 4090. Only the FP8 W8A8, W4A16 and FP8 KV paths apply.

This is NVIDIA's vendor-official PTQ. gh api returns the canonical full_name NVIDIA/Model-Optimizer, and the latest default-branch commit is a2a554c294ec on 2026-10-06.

On vLLM, the runtime already installed here, its outputs are limited. (The 2026-09-29 sweep refuted TensorRT-LLM. SGLang, an unqualified alternative in this layer, is also a ModelOpt deploy target, but its Ada FP8 support was not checked.)

Its one distinct option over vLLM's online FP8, the vendor FP8 artifact and llm-compressor's FP8_DYNAMIC is a calibrated static activation scale (plus fp8_cast KV). proposed.demonstrated_gap: macOS slot is empty: both winners are 'untested' on macos-arm64 and systemd does not run on macOS. Vendor-official route from the winner's own org: Formula/dagu.rb installs Dagu 2.18.2 from the darwin_arm64 release tarball and declares a launchd service (service do: run [opt_bin/"dagu", "start-all"], keep_alive true, log_path var/log/dagu.log). Homebrew maps 'sudo brew services' to /Library/LaunchDaemons (started at boot) and plain 'brew services' to ~/Library/LaunchAgents (started at login); Dagu's own macOS recipe is a gui-domain LaunchAgent (RunAtLoad + KeepAlive, launchctl bootstrap gui/$(id -u)) that runs only after login. The vendor route can fill the slot with the winner itself, but no evidence covers it, and the unattended boot-without-login variant is the one the host-failure gap needs. The tap ships 2.18.2 while the qualified pin is 2.16.6 and the runner rejects other versions (open gap 4), so the trial needs the new frozen 2.18.2 plan.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: Preconditions: record the Mac's FileVault state and check whether an encrypted boot stops at the unlock screen before LaunchDaemons start (if so, a failed login-less reboot case is not attributable to Dagu or launchd); confirm the installed plist lands in /Library/LaunchDaemons. Then on the 64 GB M5 Pro: install from the tap, run 'sudo brew services start dagu --sudo-service-user <operator>', and replay the frozen cases under the 2.18.2 plan: run history visible in UI/API; cancel leaves no surviving child processes; retry; catch-up of a missed cron slot (catchup_window + queues.enabled); restart after 'launchctl kickstart -k' and after a reboot with no user login; loopback bind and auth posture checked (repository advisory GHSA-6qr9-g2xw-cw92). The tap route is overturned for the macOS slot if any case fails that passes under systemd on the WSL host with the same 2.18.2 plan (for example an orphaned child after cancel, or no start after a login-less reboot); then a LaunchDaemon written from Apple's launchd specification or another supervisor must be qualified instead. The same Mac install can act as the vendor-baseline standby scheduler for the host-loss case.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: Open gap 1 (host loss, recovery on an independent host). Vendor baseline first: Dagu documents standby schedulers 'on other machines' using directory-based locking (takeover within 30 s) and catch-up replay of missed cron runs (catchup_window + queues.enabled). Inference, not stated by the doc: a lock directory seen from other machines must be shared between them, so Dagu failover keeps a shared-storage dependency; its distributed architecture also keeps 'Persistent server data' server-side (workers do not mount it). Nomad uses a cluster-level failure model instead: 'When a node is lost, Nomad replaces the allocations instead and ignores the reschedule block'; periodic batch jobs it calls 'distributed cron'; forced termination of an overrunning run (prohibit_overlap with group.max_run_duration). Not targeted now: the layer is on_requirement_change and overturn_when needs real jobs that require host-loss survival, and it adds a Nomad agent cluster across the WSL workstation and both Macs. For failed (not lost) batch allocations the default reschedule policy is attempts = 1 per 24h; lost-node replacement is governed by the disconnect block, which this sweep did not read. Also not verified: quorum sizing and process-tree containment on macOS.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: Same frozen effect/retry/recovery cases on three hosts (WSL workstation plus both Macs), Nomad against Dagu standby schedulers sharing one data directory: power off the host of the active scheduler mid-window and measure (a) whether the next cron slot fires on time on a surviving host, (b) the in-flight run's recorded outcome and the number of duplicate effects against an idempotency-keyed fake effect, (c) run-history continuity, (d) cancellation leaving no surviving child processes on Linux and macOS, (e) operator burden (daemons, config lines, upgrade steps). Nomad earns a trial only when real jobs need host-loss survival and it passes cases that Dagu's shared-directory failover fails, at acceptable burden.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: WSL is the component that starts and stops the distro, and the winners cannot cover GAP0's unattended reboot without it. (1) Start. WSL has no setting that starts a distro when Windows boots: the installed wsl.exe 3.0.1 --help lists none, the wsl-config [boot] command runs 'when the WSL instance starts', and a keyword scan of the 2.9.11 to 3.0.2 release notes found none. Microsoft's maintainer recommends Task Scheduler running wsl.exe (#10828). The host has a Task Scheduler task 'WSL NativeStack2604 start' that the repository does not record. It uses a logon trigger with a 30 s delay, logon type Interactive, and the action C:\Windows\System32\wsl.exe -d NativeStack2604 --exec /bin/true. An interactive-token task runs 'only in an existing interactive session', so a reboot with no logon (a Windows Update restart or the return of AC power) starts nothing. On 2026-10-06 the task ran at 13:48:35Z, 19 s after the distro's PID 1 (13:48:16Z). An unidentified component had already started the distro. Inside the distro the chain works: linger is on, dagu.service is enabled, and user@1000 and Dagu's scheduler were up at 13:48:27Z. (2) Stop. In the source, the guest gets at most boot.initTimeout (10 s by default) between systemctl poweroff and reboot(RB_POWER_OFF), and the host waits at most 30 s. dagu.service inherits TimeoutStopSec=90 s. One Windows restart was observed. Its systemd shutdown transaction began at 13:47:02.746Z, Dagu stopped gracefully at 13:47:02.826Z with no run evident, and user@1000 never logged as stopped. The persistent journal ends at 13:47:03.886Z with no final shutdown target, so the teardown was cut about 1.1 s in, before the guest's fallback, by an unidentified cause. The real window at a Windows restart has not been measured. PR #41688's 30 s change applies to the WSLC session VM, not the distro VM (per code search of the default branch). No receipt covers a reboot, or a stop with a run in flight.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn:
Operator reboot drill on the linux-wsl2 workstation: 3 restarts per arm, with nobody logging on for 10 minutes.
- Arm A: the existing logon task (status quo).
- Arm B: the same action under an At startup trigger with an S4U principal (New-ScheduledTaskPrincipal -LogonType S4U, no stored password).
- Arm C: no task.

For each restart, record:
- Windows LastBootUpTime, the distro's PID 1 start and the dagu.service start, from the journal;
- which component started the distro (the task's LastRunTime against PID 1);
- whether a DAG slot that fell inside the downtime runs exactly once (Dagu catch-up, #2742).

In arm B, check interop (cmd.exe /d /c ver), /mnt/c and /dev/dxg both before and after the interactive logon. With instanceIdleTimeout=-1, the instance started before logon serves the whole session, and #8643 was closed for inactivity, not fixed.

B replaces A if Dagu is running with no logon in 3/3 restarts, interop and the GPU work after logon, and no slot runs twice. If S4U fails, test TASK_LOGON_PASSWORD, or autologon with arm A.

Stop side: restart Windows while a DAG step traps SIGTERM and appends an fsync'd timestamp every 0.5 s. The last timestamp gives the real stop window. Compare boot.initTimeout 10000 against 25000 only if that window comes out near 10 s. If it stays near the observed 1.1 s, the lever is a Windows-side step that stops the distro before shutdown, which was not researched.
evidence: https://github.com/microsoft/WSL/issues/10828#issuecomment-1828283311: a Microsoft member (2023-11-27) says WSL has no direct way to autostart a distro and recommends Task Scheduler to start wsl.exe.

https://github.com/MicrosoftDocs/WSL/blob/main/WSL/wsl-config.md (ms.date 04/15/2026, fetched 2026-10-06): the [boot] keys are command ('run when the WSL instance starts'), protectBinfmt, systemd and initTimeout (default 10000 ms). [general] instanceIdleTimeout set to -1 disables auto shutdown. No key starts a distro at Windows boot.

https://github.com/microsoft/WSL/blob/3.0.1/src/linux/init/init.cpp#L2829-L2846: on a terminate-instance request from the service (InitTerminateInstance, lines 2755-2774), init runs 'systemctl poweroff' in a detached thread, sleeps Config.BootInitTimeout, then calls reboot(RB_POWER_OFF).
https://github.com/microsoft/WSL/blob/3.0.1/src/linux/init/WslDistributionConfig.h#L61: BootInitTimeout = 10 * 1000. WslDistributionConfig.cpp#L56 maps it to the wsl.conf key boot.initTimeout.

https://github.com/microsoft/WSL/blob/3.0.1/src/windows/service/exe/WslCoreVm.h#L34-L35: UTILITY_VM_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT and UTILITY_VM_TERMINATE_TIMEOUT are both 30 * 1000. WslCoreVm.cpp#L746-L777 waits that long for a clean VM exit before calling TerminateComputeSystem.

https://github.com/microsoft/WSL/pull/41688/files: the 3.0.1 '30 seconds' change edits only HcsVirtualMachine.cpp (a wait of 5000 becomes 30000 ms). GitHub code search of the default branch finds HcsVirtualMachine referenced only by WSLCSessionManager.cpp, the WSLC session VM.

https://github.com/microsoft/WSL/pull/41460 (2.9.13): COM now retries activation of a stopping wslservice instead of failing with Wsl/E_OUTOFMEMORY. This matters when a start task races a service that is stopping.

https://github.com/microsoft/WSL/blob/3.0.1/src/windows/inc/comservicehelper.h#L395-L397: the service accepts SERVICE_CONTROL_SHUTDOWN only when it defines OnSystemShutdown, and code search finds that name only in this template. This is a lead, not proof, about how Windows shutdown reaches the distro.
https://github.com/microsoft/WSL/issues/8643#issuecomment-1921175483: 'Interop is broken when WSL is started prior to user logon' was closed by the inactivity bot, not fixed.

https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/taskschd/principal-logontype: TASK_LOGON_S4U stores no password and has no access to the network or to encrypted files. TASK_LOGON_INTERACTIVE_TOKEN runs a task only in an existing interactive session.
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/taskschd/task-triggers: event-based triggers can start a task when the system starts up or when a user logs on.

https://github.com/microsoft/WSL/releases/tag/3.0.1: 3.0.1, released 2026-09-29, is the latest stable release; 3.0.2 (2026-10-05) is a prerelease. Commit ffb4e1869684 landed on the default branch on 2026-10-06.

Host observation (NativeStack2604, 2026-10-06, read-only, no URL):
- WSL: wsl.exe --version reports 3.0.1.0, and --help offers no autostart option.
- Task: MSFT_TaskLogonTrigger with delay PT30S, LogonType Interactive, LastRunTime 13:48:35Z.
- Current boot (UTC): Windows LastBootUpTime 13:47:49Z; VM kernel 13:48:10Z; distro PID 1 13:48:16Z; user@1000 and dagu.service started 13:48:27Z.
- Units: Linger=yes. dagu.service has TimeoutStopUSec=1min 30s and KillMode=control-group.
- Previous boot: PID 1 began its shutdown transaction at 13:47:02.746Z. Dagu logged 'All services stopped gracefully' at 13:47:02.826Z. Stopping user@1000 began at 13:47:02.798Z and never logged as stopped. The journal's last entry is at 13:47:03.886Z, with no final shutdown target.
proposed.source: Vendor-official pass on the follow-up's search directions. Sources: gh api for releases, PRs, code search and source at tag 3.0.1, plus maintainer issue comments; MicrosoftDocs and Microsoft Learn pages; the installed wsl.exe 3.0.1; and read-only host probes on NativeStack2604 (schtasks, Get-ScheduledTask, loginctl, systemctl, journalctl).

proposed.demonstrated_gap:
Nothing signals a power loss. A grep of docs, evidence, adoption, blueprints, catalogs and manifests finds no UPS or networkupstools reference, and whether the workstation has a UPS is unknown.

For a USB HID UPS, the vendor-native baseline is Windows itself: a HID battery miniport for USB-attached UPS devices, plus the critical battery action 'Shut Down'. That route ends in the same WSL teardown at Windows shutdown, which one restart showed cut about 1.1 s in.

NUT covers what that baseline lacks:
- network or SNMP UPSes;
- one UPS signalling several hosts, including the Macs;
- a pre-shutdown hook (upsmon SHUTDOWNCMD) that could terminate the distro, giving systemctl poweroff its initTimeout, before Windows starts its own shutdown.

v2.8.5 (2026-04-03) ships official NUT-for-Windows x86_64 archives. Its release notes record two problems: the first archive's upsmon could not start because NSS DLLs were missing (the archive was republished), and the Windows libwinhid backend for usbhid-ups is experimental and read-only. Whether a command run under NUT's Windows service account can reach the user's per-user distro is untested.

NUT is maintained: commit 1a8369f86884 landed on the default branch on 2026-10-02.
evidence: https://github.com/networkupstools/nut/releases/tag/v2.8.5: released 2026-04-03 with the assets NUT-for-Windows-x86_64-RELEASE-2.8.5.7z and -1-fixNSS.7z. The notes record an errata (the first Windows archive's upsmon could not start for missing NSS DLLs), an experimental read-only libwinhid backend for usbhid-ups on Windows, and fixes to Windows service startup.
https://github.com/networkupstools/nut/commit/1a8369f86884: a commit on the default branch (master) dated 2026-10-02, so the repository is maintained within the 90-day window.

https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/design/component-guidelines/power-and-charging-subsystem-implementation: 'A Human Interface Device (HID) battery miniport driver for USB-attached Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS) devices is supported'. This is the vendor-native baseline to name before NUT.

https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/customize/power-settings/battery-settings-critical-battery-action: critical battery action value 3, 'Shut Down', shuts the system down when the critical battery level is reached (PowerCfg BATACTIONCRIT, GUID <session-id>).

https://github.com/nutdotnet/WinNUT-Client: the common third-party Windows NUT client is stale. Its default branch, dev-2.3, has no commit since 2026-07-08 (last push 2026-04-25), so the NUT arm uses NUT's own Windows upsmon.
proposed.source: Seeded by the follow-up brief (networkupstools/nut@1a8369f86884). Verified with gh api (repository, releases/latest, the v2.8.5 notes, commits since 2026-07-08) and compared against the Windows-native HID UPS baseline on Microsoft Learn.

claude_discover.notes:
FOLLOW-UP ON GAP0 (linux-wsl2). Three premises in the brief were checked against primary sources, using fp-check's step of restating each claim.

(1) "Nothing starts the distro after a reboot" is partly wrong.
- The host has a Task Scheduler task 'WSL NativeStack2604 start' that the repository does not record. A grep for the task name, 'exec /bin/true', TaskLogonTrigger, ScheduledTask and "logon trigger" in docs, adoption, evidence, catalogs, blueprints and manifests found nothing relevant.
- The task uses a logon trigger with a 30 s delay and logon type Interactive. It cannot fire without a logon, so the unattended-reboot case remains open.
- On 2026-10-06 Windows booted at 13:47:49Z and the distro's PID 1 started at 13:48:16Z. The task ran at 13:48:35Z, 19 s later, so another component started the distro.
- That starter is unidentified. Project memory names the Codex desktop app's wsl_remote_connections (switched off 19:59Z), Windows Terminal profiles and Explorer navigation to the distro share as uncontrolled starters. None was verified here.

(2) "Linger exists only as a draft" is out of date for the host.
- Linger=yes. dagu.service is an enabled user unit (WantedBy=default.target, Restart=always) running dagu start-all 2.18.2.
- Only a repository receipt is missing. docs/decisions/2026-10-05-trading-unattended-hosting-recovery.md:207-208 already documents linger and its WSL caveat.

(3) "WSL 3.0.1 raised the VM termination timeout to 30 s (#41688)" is misattributed.
- #41688 edits HcsVirtualMachine.cpp. Code search of the default branch finds that class used only by WSLCSessionManager.cpp, the WSLC session VM.
- The distro's own limits at 3.0.1 are on two levels:
  - Host: UTILITY_VM_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT and UTILITY_VM_TERMINATE_TIMEOUT, both 30 s (WslCoreVm.h:34-35).
  - Guest: systemctl poweroff, with a fallback to reboot(RB_POWER_OFF) after boot.initTimeout (init.cpp:2829-2846). That defaults to 10 s (WslDistributionConfig.h:61); the docs describe it only as the systemd start wait. The host's /etc/wsl.conf does not set it.
- These are upper bounds, not a measured window. Against them sit dagu.service's inherited TimeoutStopSec of 90 s (DefaultTimeoutStopUSec is 1min 30s for both managers) and Dagu's default MaxCleanUpTime of 5 s (dagucloud/dagu@v2.18.2 internal/ir/dag.go:515, 528-529).
- One Windows restart was observed (about 13:47Z on 2026-10-06), with no Dagu run evident:
  - Systemd began a shutdown transaction at 13:47:02.746Z.
  - Dagu stopped gracefully at 13:47:02.826Z.
  - user@1000 never logged as stopped.
  - The persistent journal ends at 13:47:03.886Z with no final shutdown target.
- So something cut the teardown about 1.1 s in, before the guest's 10 s fallback. Raising initTimeout may therefore change nothing until the real window is measured.
- How Windows shutdown reaches WSL is unknown. Code search finds OnSystemShutdown only in the comservicehelper.h template.
- #41460 (2.9.13) does what the brief says.

WINNER HEALTH
- dagucloud/dagu: latest v2.18.2 (2026-10-04), not archived, GPL-3.0 (information only).
  - The host runs 2.18.2, but this layer's winner pin is still 2.16.6 (the trading hold; see docs/decisions/2026-10-05-dagu-mise-pin-move.md).
  - 2.18.2 has shutdown fixes that 2.16.6 lacks: #2966 (keep SIGTERM handled during supervisor shutdown), #2972 (run coordinator shutdown on SIGINT and SIGTERM) and #2885 (optional signal propagation to running DAG processes).
  - Catch-up recovery (#2742) arrived in 2.16.4.
  - start-all runs a zombie detector at a 45 s interval (host journal).
- systemd: upstream v262 (2026-09-22) was not compared with the distro's 255.4-1ubuntu8.17.
- microsoft/WSL: the installed 3.0.1 is the latest stable release. 3.0.2 (2026-10-05) is a prerelease. It includes #41780, which restores WSL's binfmt_misc entry when systemd-binfmt overrides it; that matters for interop on systemd distros.

INCUMBENCY: Dagu and systemd hold GAP0's host-failure modalities on local_integration evidence alone. No receipt covers a reboot, a power loss or a stop with a run in flight; the trading hosting decision, lines 368-370, lists host reboot and catch-up as open.

NOT PROPOSED
- nutdotnet/WinNUT-Client: stale (no commit on its default branch since 2026-07-08).
- healthchecks/healthchecks, TwiN/gatus and louislam/uptime-kuma: external dead-man's switches, the only class that notices a host that never comes back. They were already judged, and this round gathered no new upstream evidence.
- launchd: belongs to the macOS slot, outside GAP0's linux-wsl2 scope.
- Windows service wrappers (WinSW, NSSM, Servy, shawl): not researched. Starting the distro is a one-shot, idempotent wsl.exe call that Task Scheduler (the vendor's recommendation) covers. A repetition trigger on the same task would also restart the distro after a VM crash or wsl --shutdown.
- Sysinternals Autologon with the existing logon task: an alternative arm if S4U fails; it is a closed-source vendor tool with no repository.
- Residuals with no repository:
  - The BIOS setting for restoring power after AC loss is unknown.
  - Without a UPS, power loss stays an accepted residual.
  - A Windows-side step that stops the distro before shutdown (for example a logoff script) was not researched.

CALLS AND SKILLS
- The gh_api budget is fully spent (40/40). web_fetch counts 6 requests, one of them a cache hit.
- Host probes were read-only: wsl.exe --version, --help and -l -v; schtasks /query; Get-ScheduledTask; loginctl; systemctl show; journalctl. No candidate code ran.
- supply-chain-risk-auditor was loaded, but its collector does not apply: the candidates are C and C++ projects with no npm, PyPI or Go manifests. Its rule that unassessable data is not evidence of risk was applied, and maintenance was measured with gh api commits?since=2026-07-08.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: Qualify the official WSL runtime together with native Windows Task Scheduler as the missing Windows-to-distro startup path. The documented idle settings and Linux user-service linger do not establish recovery after Windows reboots. WSL 3.0.1 also contains a relevant shutdown improvement: its VM termination wait increased from 5 to 30 seconds. This complements Dagu/systemd on linux-wsl2; application recovery within that window remains unmeasured.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: Freeze an identified real research/simulation workflow, inputs and Dagu/systemd pins. Compare the existing configuration with Windows AtStartup and AtLogOn tasks launching the named distro under its owning Windows account, with the Dagu user unit enabled and linger qualified separately. Across 10 physical reboots per arm, require exactly one service instance, readable run history and readiness within five minutes of the relevant trigger. AtLogOn cannot satisfy recovery before login. Separately compare the installed WSL version with 3.0.1 under identical workload and shutdown conditions: require checkpoint/stop receipts within a proposed 25-second budget, no corrupted committed artifacts and no duplicate completed effects. Record Windows task history, WSL diagnostics, systemd journal and Dagu history. Reject unattended qualification if account access requires an unapproved credential change or shutdown receipts fail. These are proposed tests, not executed results.
evidence: Canonical owner, creation in 2016, stars, pushed_at, archived=false and MIT license: [GitHub repository metadata](https://api.github.com/repos/microsoft/WSL).

The required default-branch query returned ffb4e186968486d297cd8792af3714fbb07f459e, committed on 2026-10-06; maintenance is established independently of pushed_at: [90-day commit query](https://api.github.com/repos/microsoft/WSL/commits?since=2026-07-08T00:00:00Z&per_page=1).
Latest stable release 3.0.1 was published on 2026-09-29 and supplies official x64 and ARM64 installers: [release](https://github.com/microsoft/WSL/releases/tag/3.0.1).

The patch changes HcsVirtualMachine teardown from a 5-second wait to 30 seconds; its motivation includes pending operations not being flushed under pressure. This is not proof that Dagu receives 30 seconds during Windows shutdown: [PR 41688](https://github.com/microsoft/WSL/pull/41688), [patch](https://api.github.com/repos/microsoft/WSL/pulls/41688/files).

Release 2.9.13 includes the stopping-service activation fix. The PR corrects misleading OOM handling and describes retries that can take minutes, rather than guaranteeing prompt recovery: [release](https://github.com/microsoft/WSL/releases/tag/2.9.13), [PR 41460](https://github.com/microsoft/WSL/pull/41460).

The pinned documentation defines boot.command as executing when the WSL instance starts. The stack's decision records disabled idle termination and linger only as a draft: [WSL configuration at 7ea1c6f9e25f](https://github.com/MicrosoftDocs/WSL/blob/7ea1c6f9e25f/WSL/wsl-config.md), [stack decision](https://github.com/seathatflowsinourveins/native-agent-stack/blob/main/docs/decisions/2026-10-01-new-wsl-distro-recipe.md#L146-L218).

Microsoft documents distinct startup/logon triggers, task security principals, per-Windows-user distro ownership and explicit distro selection: [task triggers](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/scheduledtasks/new-scheduledtasktrigger?view=windowsserver2025-ps), [task principals](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/scheduledtasks/new-scheduledtaskprincipal?view=windowsserver2025-ps), [WSL ownership](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/wsl/setup/environment), [WSL commands](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/basic-commands).

The v255 manual says linger starts a user manager at Linux boot and retains it after logout. This addresses the guest user-manager lifecycle: [loginctl source](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/v255/man/loginctl.xml#L185-L198).
proposed.source: Follow-up critic's Windows boot/shutdown seeds; verified against Microsoft's repository API, release notes, patch and official Windows documentation. Task Scheduler is the native Windows baseline represented alongside WSL, not a separately proposed open-source scheduler.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: Conditional power-loss complement: if a compatible UPS exists, NUT can observe power state and initiate a configured Windows shutdown before battery exhaustion. UPS presence, compatibility and available runtime are unknown. Compare first against Windows' native battery policy and any existing UPS-manufacturer shutdown integration. NUT's Windows support is documented as experimental, and its local monitor authentication adds configuration cost. Its older release is not stale: default-branch activity was verified in October.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: First establish the UPS model, connection and runtime under workstation load. Reuse upstream NIT/dummy-ups for software signalling tests, then compare the existing native/manufacturer control with the corrected official Windows v2.8.5 package on the same hardware. Exercise sustained outage, power restoration, communication loss and low-battery shutdown. Require timely detection within two configured polling intervals, ordinary Windows shutdown while sufficient reserve remains, successful WSL/Dagu stop receipts within the qualified shutdown budget, and intact committed simulation artifacts after restart. Prefer the existing control if it passes equally with less operational burden. Promote NUT only if its measured improvement justifies the service and local authentication configuration. Without a UPS, retain abrupt power loss as an accepted GAP0 residual.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: This gap is specific to the WSL host and sits in the worktree winner. Worktrunk's own docs say cache sharing is copy-free only where reflinks exist ('APFS (macOS), btrfs and XFS (Linux), ReFS (Windows)'), and 'On ext4 and NTFS, which have no reflink, every file is copied in full'. Their table gives 2 min and 14 GB for each full copy of a 14 GB target/. The WSL2 workstation's home is ext4 (observed with df -T), so every Rust or Cython worker worktree (a NautilusTrader-class target/) pays either a full copy or a cold build. Treehouse keeps a pool of reusable worktrees 'with dependencies and build cache intact' (README L24). It reuses a worktree only when it is idle, unleased, clean, and its HEAD is merged into the reset target (L112-L114). It records immutable durable leases that keep a worktree out of get and prune until released (L157). It counts tracked changes and untracked files as dirty even when repository config hides untracked files from git status (L161). These are the edit-ownership cases this layer must preserve; under open gap 1, worktrunk's dirty-removal refusal was observed only on 0.78.0. There is no gap on the Macs, where APFS reflinks apply.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: On the WSL2 ext4 host, compare worktrunk 0.80.0 (wt switch -c plus wt step copy-ignored) with treehouse v3.1.2 (treehouse get, then return to pool) for 4 parallel worker worktrees of the NautilusTrader checkout. Measure wall time and disk delta until each worktree is ready with a warm target/, and the first incremental cargo build time. Run frozen ownership cases where each tool must refuse reuse or removal: a tracked dirty change, an untracked file with status.showUntrackedFiles=no, an unpushed commit, and an active lease. Treehouse is retained only if it saves time and disk materially and passes every ownership case. Any lost edit, or a saving that is small next to the task, keeps worktrunk.

output.notes:
Scope and acceptance: This discovery serves independently reviewed US-equities historical-simulation work for NautilusTrader, with LEAN comparison; no live trading. No installation, candidate execution, credential inspection, benchmark, or adoption occurred. Proposed trials should use the mandated Inspect/Harbor harness, a frozen task and independent acceptance. Current winners have local-integration evidence, but the supplied layer contains no executed head-to-head establishing their superiority. Their ranking therefore remains a provisional control, not a measured best.

Native baseline and winner health: Codex rust-v0.160.1 supplies agents, exec, review, queue, resume, fork, sandbox, and app-server commands in its [tagged CLI source](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.160.1/codex-rs/cli/src/main.rs). Its [latest patch](https://github.com/openai/codex/releases/tag/rust-v0.160.1) concerns remote Windows MCP environment preservation; no new worker-quality result justified re-proposing this already-judged repository. Installed --help/settings could not be inspected in this web-only lane, so this is source verification, not an installed-client qualification. Claude's current release is 2.1.292, beyond the input's 2.1.291 snapshot. Both winner APIs report their existing canonical names and archived=false; neither shows a major-version transition. License-history/relicensing was not audited.

Vendor discovery: The two requested organization REST listings were inaccessible. The [OpenAI](https://github.com/orgs/openai/repositories?type=all&sort=updated) and [Anthropic](https://github.com/orgs/anthropics/repositories?type=all&sort=updated) pages displayed Last pushed listings. Relevant results included Codex, OpenAI Agents Python/JS, Claude Code, and Claude Agent SDK Python/TypeScript. This was bounded listing coverage, not an exhaustive organization inventory. OpenAI's codex-plugin-cc was not requalified within budget; its maintenance remains unverified here, not stale by inference.

A Linear account is therefore not a universal requirement. The same source says approval-blocked state is memory-only and lost on orchestrator restart. [The README](https://github.com/openai/symphony/blob/main/README.md) still describes an engineering preview. It is not re-proposed: no retained outcome evidence establishes an advantage for this bounded-worker requirement, and the checked recovery limitation does not close the known durability gap. Its default-branch maintenance was not queried; pushed_at was not substituted for that check.

Other named workspace seeds: [superset-sh/superset](https://github.com/superset-sh/superset/releases) remains at the seeded desktop-v1.36.0, with Linux x64 and macOS arm64 assets; [its installation documentation](https://github.com/superset-sh/superset/blob/main/apps/docs/content/docs/install.mdx) calls Linux experimental. No new outcome evidence reopened it. [Microsoft Agent Framework's release notes](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-framework/releases) contain relevant checkpoint and failure-propagation fixes; surfaced shell-result issue reports were not source-verified and were not used to reject it. Method and limits: All six proposed repositories predate the 90-day cutoff and returned a default-branch commit inside the window. A per_page=1 query proves nonzero activity, not weekly cadence or a top Scorecard score. Stars and licenses did not determine fit. Skills were read at the exact upstream pins in the [stack manifest](https://github.com/seathatflowsinourveins/native-agent-stack/blob/main/adoption/skills/manifest.json), because local files were inaccessible. Supply-chain and false-positive guidance informed evidence boundaries; no collector or exploit-verification workflow ran, and no clean security verdict is claimed. Counts include failed requests; GitHub API URL requests are counted under gh_api rather than web_fetch. All research budgets were exhausted.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: The layer's typed-application fixture is held at TypeScript 5.9.3 by its OpenAPI type generator. receipt.json:117 and experiment.json:247 record that TypeScript 7.0.2 'does not satisfy openapi-typescript7.13.0 peer ^5.x and lacks the JS ts.factory API used by that generator' (README.md:36-39). The incumbent has not moved: openapi-typescript's HEAD package.json (last default-branch commit 2026-09-25) is still 7.13.0 with peer typescript ^5.x, which rules out TypeScript 6 as well. The winner no longer blocks the upgrade. The Next.js 16.4.0 useTypeScriptCli page says next build runs the project-local tsc, which 'supports TypeScript 6 and enables TypeScript 7'; the page marks this as experimental. The FastAPI maintainers' own full-stack template generates its typed client with @hey-api/openapi-ts 0.97.3 under TypeScript ^6.0.3. @hey-api/openapi-ts 0.99.0 (npm latest) declares no TypeScript peer, and its @hey-api/codegen-core 0.9.1 depends only on @hey-api/types and c12, so neither recorded failure cause applies. proposed.demonstrated_gap:
GAP3 (open_gaps[3]) reads 'No container lane (Docker/Compose, Podman/Quadlet, Dev Containers) has been run against this workload, so native versus container is unmeasured.' The only executed container evidence is rootless Podman from 2026-09-23. Those receipts predate the new distro, which the 2026-10-01 review still records as not created, so they do not certify this host. The same review lists WSLc as a 'WSL3.0.1 GA currency candidate; unmeasured OCI/container workload fit'. It says a container requirement must choose among WSLc, Docker/Compose and Podman, and its next_wave is to 'compare WSLc/Docker/Podman volumes, loopback ports and shutdown recovery; restore one owned database independently'. The input JSON omits WSLc. WSLc is the host-platform vendor's own lane and is already on this host. wsl.exe --version reports 3.0.1.0, and wslc.exe, wslcsession.exe and container.exe are in C:\Program Files\WSL; none were executed. A trial therefore installs no second engine, which answers hosting-container-practice.md line 29. Architecture (deep dive):
- A per-user wslcsession.exe owns each session's VM and its storage VHD under %AppData%\Local\wslc\sessions.
- Windows-path volumes are virtiofs shares, and ports are published through the new Consommé networking.
- At tag 3.0.1 the session talks to a Docker Engine API socket (/var/run/docker.sock) inside the VM.
Limits today:
- No Compose. The GA post calls it the top request and says work on it has started, so this lane runs each container with wslc run on a network from wslc network create.
- No DOCKER_HOST endpoint (microsoft/WSL#40976 is open), so docker/compose cannot drive WSLc.
- Windows only. apple/container is the Mac counterpart and was already judged.
- No restart policy or GPU access is described in the GA post or the deep dive. Both are unknown, not shown absent.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn:
Run every arm on this host in one session: native, WSLc 3.0.1 GA, and Podman as well if the coordinator installs it for the 2026-10-01 next_wave. The 2026-09-23 Podman numbers are context only. The workload is the gap-wave3 one, unchanged: digest-pinned postgres:18.6-alpine plus the python:3.13-slim app image. On WSLc, start each container with wslc run on one wslc network. Keep PostgreSQL data on a named volume inside the session VHD, not on a Windows-path -v bind over virtiofs; the README records that an earlier Documents-directory bind mount stalled before guest boot. Measure per arm:
- build, start and ready times.
- The unchanged alembic upgrade and 12 pytest API checks, run from inside the WSL distro against Consommé-published ports. Reachability under mirrored networking is itself a check.
- Persistence across wslc container restart, session/VM shutdown (3.0.1 raised the VM termination timeout to 30 s) and a Windows reboot.
- Kill recovery. Check restart-policy support first. If WSLc has none, record a manual restart and mark kill recovery not comparable.
- pg_dump/pg_restore into an independent database, with matching row counts and checksums.
- CPU and memory under a fixed sustained load from the selected generator (Locust, if adopted).
- Cleanup of the session VHD.
WSLc is overturned if any of these hold:
- a check fails only on WSLc;
- published ports are unreachable from the distro;
- data is lost across a shutdown;
- start, recovery or resource cost is worse than the same-session Podman arm, or worse than native by a margin fixed before the run, with no offsetting gain.
If port forwarding or disk permissions misbehave, re-test on 3.0.2 once it reaches GA. proposed.demonstrated_gap: This is the measurement step of the layer's own container comparison, not a production load test. The 2026-09-23 refutation of grafana/k6 said a production load test presupposes production hosting and an SLO. That premise is not in play here. The layer's next_action requires qualifying a host or container option on 'measured workload cost'. hosting-container-practice.md lines 38-44 require the same locked checks, including resources, when a container lane is compared with native. The only native-versus-container resource figures, from the gap-wave3 Podman receipt, 'are single-sample snapshots via ps/podman stats/top, not sustained-load averages'. No load generator is in the catalog. A grep of catalogs/, manifests/, docs/ and evidence/ at ecfa1127 on 2026-10-06 found locustio/locust nowhere. grafana/k6 appears only as the refuted 2026-09-23 candidate record (manifest-20260923, saturation ledger, sweep inputs and returns). Without a fixed, repeatable load, the targeted WSLc/native (and Podman) comparison cannot measure workload cost. The same instrument would later measure the latency a TLS edge adds, if that trigger fires. Locust fits the winner's toolchain: it is Python like the FastAPI winner, and locustfiles are plain Python driving the same routes. The 2.46.7 docs cover headless runs with -u/-r/--run-time and an exit code driven by a p95 threshold. The 2.46.7 runner warns when its own CPU passes 90%, so saturation of the load generator itself is observable.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn:
Fix the arms before running. Use one Locust 2.46.7 locustfile, pinned in the fixture's uv lock, that exercises the fixture's 12 API routes. Hold the read/write mix, users, spawn rate and run time fixed (for example 3 runs of 10 minutes). Run it against native, WSLc and Podman (if installed) on this host in one session. Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, failure rate and requests per second from Locust, plus server-side CPU and memory sampled over the whole run. Locust is overturned as the instrument if either holds:
- its CPU warning fires on a single process before the FastAPI fixture saturates at the trial load, so distributed mode would be needed just to drive the fixture;
- repeat runs of one arm vary beyond a tolerance fixed in advance (proposed: p95 coefficient of variation above 10%).
In either case, a compiled constant-arrival-rate generator becomes the comparator at the same rate. The named comparator is grafana/k6, which was refuted on scope, not quality.
