proposed.demonstrated_gap:
GAP1 (open_gaps[1]) reads: 'No production authentication, hosted deployment, production load test or cloud hosting is established. The PostgreSQL build is a synthetic loopback trust-auth fixture without TLS'. The PostgreSQL clause is already partly answered. A 2026-09-23 receipt rebuilt 18.6 with OpenSSL and enforced scram-sha-256 and loopback TLS, using 'a locally generated fixture cert, not from any CA'. What remains without TLS is the HTTP edge: Next.js and FastAPI serve plain HTTP. Today that edge has no consumer. The fixture binds loopback only: next start --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port 18080 (package.json line 12), uvicorn --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18081 (serve.py line 33), and the API is reached through a same-origin rewrite to 127.0.0.1:18081 (next.config.ts line 6). WSL mirrored networking, verified 'mirrored', would expose only listeners bound beyond loopback. A TLS edge therefore presupposes a LAN-client, remote-service or production-authentication requirement, and the layer has not chosen one. That is why this is compare, not targeted. When the trigger fires, Caddy is the strongest answer verified here.
- Vendor baseline: FastAPI 0.142.2 docs prescribe one TLS Termination Proxy and name Traefik and Caddy as the two that 'can also handle certificate renewals'. Next.js 16.3.8 offers HTTPS only through next dev --experimental-https (mkcert), and documents that flag as development-only.
- Caddy issues certificates for loopback, IP and .localhost/.local/.internal/.home.arpa names from its own local CA (Smallstep libraries). It needs no ACME, DNS validation, account or credential, installs its root into the local trust store and renews intermediates automatically.
- Traefik's v3.7 TLS reference offers only ACME or user-supplied certificates. Nginx and HAProxy were not checked in this lane.
Prior record: Caddy is held as discovery_only (catalogs/landscape/independent-discovery.json /candidates/44: primary-source review, no local runtime or comparative measurement), with no refuter verdict. Pin v2.11.7 or later. 2.11.6 panicked when reverse-proxying HTTP/2 request bodies and cut off streaming/SSE responses at 60 s. The local CA 'is trusted only where the CA's root certificate is installed', and the automatic install reaches only the WSL Linux store, so the root must also be distributed to Windows and Mac clients.

https://caddyserver.com/docs/automatic-https#local-https — 'To serve non-public sites over HTTPS, Caddy generates its own certificate authority (CA)', stored at pki/authorities/local. 'Local HTTPS does not use ACME nor does it perform any DNS validation. It works only on the local machine and is trusted only where the CA's root certificate is installed.'

https://caddyserver.com/docs/automatic-https#hostname-requirements — localhost (including the .localhost, .local, .internal and .home.arpa TLDs) and IP addresses do not qualify for publicly-trusted certificates, so they are served from the local CA.

https://caddyserver.com/docs/automatic-https#ca-root — on first use Caddy tries to install the root into the system trust store(s). skip_install_trust disables this, caddy trust retries it and caddy untrust removes it. Intermediates are short-lived and renewed automatically (#ca-intermediates).

proposed.demonstrated_gap: Traefik is the vendor baseline. FastAPI's HTTPS docs name it first. The FastAPI maintainers' template, at e99fbaeba3b5, runs Traefik on Docker labels with an ACME certificate resolver (--certificatesresolvers.le.acme.tlschallenge=true) for Host(...${DOMAIN}) routes. It shares Caddy's trigger: the fixture binds loopback only, and no LAN-client, remote-service or production-authentication requirement is recorded. Once the trigger fires, this requirement involves loopback and LAN names with no public domain and no new account. For that case, the v3.7 TLS-certificates reference defers automated certificates to its Let's Encrypt (ACME) page. Otherwise it accepts only user-supplied certificates through the file provider and falls back to a generated default certificate. That reference shows no built-in local CA; this is a finding from the reference, not a verified absence. On these hosts Traefik therefore needs an external certificate source, such as mkcert or a private ACME CA, to match Caddy's local HTTPS. Its own advantages are label-driven dynamic routing for a Compose or Podman lane and ACME for a public domain; neither is selected. Security cadence is active. Three high-severity advisories (request smuggling, header-sanitization bypass via trailers, path-scope bypass) were published on 2026-09-07 and patched in v3.7.13, and v3.7.14 shipped on 2026-10-06.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: The fixture lacks demonstrated application-edge HTTPS and certificate-lifecycle acceptance for FastAPI and Next.js. Caddy supplies automatic local-CA certificates for loopback addresses and internal/LAN names without a public-domain account. Linux amd64 and macOS arm64 release assets make a bounded trial feasible. This complements the application servers; it does not establish PostgreSQL TLS, application authentication, or production readiness.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: Compare Caddy v2.11.7 with direct native HTTP and Traefik using identical routes and workloads. Require existing application checks to pass, trusted clients to validate certificates, untrusted clients to fail validation, correct proxy headers, successful certificate-state restoration, and uninterrupted representative streaming responses. Measure p95/p99 latency, errors, CPU/RSS and configuration effort over repeated runs. Prefer another proxy if it passes the same checks with materially lower operating effort or resource cost.
evidence: [FastAPI HTTPS guidance](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/deployment/https/) explicitly names Caddy and Traefik as TLS termination options; [Next.js self-hosting guidance](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/self-hosting) recommends a reverse proxy.

[Caddy automatic HTTPS](https://caddyserver.com/docs/automatic-https) documents local/internal-name and IP certificates, its local CA, persistent certificate storage, and the requirement to distribute root trust to other clients.
[Reverse-proxy quick start](https://caddyserver.com/docs/quick-starts/reverse-proxy) documents proxying to an existing local HTTP application.

[Latest-release API](https://api.github.com/repos/caddyserver/caddy/releases/latest) identifies v2.11.7, published 2026-10-03, with Linux amd64/macOS arm64 assets and fixes for HTTP/2 crashes and prematurely terminated streams.
[Repository API](https://api.github.com/repos/caddyserver/caddy) supplies canonical ownership, creation date, stars, pushed_at, archive status and Apache-2.0 license.

output.notes:
Scope: these recommendations serve reproducible local US-equities research and historical-simulation services. No installations, candidate execution, account creation or live-trading work occurred. Trial thresholds above are proposed acceptance criteria, not measured results. Research stopped at the budget limits; counts include failed requests and GitHub reads for skills and evidence, with API requests counted separately from ordinary page fetches.

Corrections verified this turn: the statement that no container lane has run is outdated. The [build/start receipt](https://github.com/seathatflowsinourveins/native-agent-stack/blob/main/evidence/artifacts/gap-wave3-20260923/hosting-services/container-build-start-resource-vs-native.json) records an executed rootless Podman FastAPI/PostgreSQL subset with 12 passing tests, but excludes Next.js/browser acceptance and retains mostly summary measurements. The [recovery receipt](https://github.com/seathatflowsinourveins/native-agent-stack/blob/main/evidence/artifacts/gap-wave3-20260923/hosting-services/container-recovery-isolation-cpu-mem-vs-native.json) explicitly corrects the earlier claim of a matched native/container comparison. These establish partial evidence, not container superiority. The build receipt also references an earlier hardened-postgres-tls-scram run; that exact receipt was not read within this budget, so blanket absence of database TLS must not be repeated as a current verified fact.

TLS boundary: [PostgreSQL's native TLS documentation](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/ssl-tcp.html) already supplies the database-side capability, subject to build and configuration acceptance. Caddy or Traefik in front of HTTP services does not qualify that connection or replace database authentication. Likewise, [Tailscale's supported custom-control-server path](https://tailscale.com/docs/how-to/set-up-custom-control-server) disproves an unconditional hosted-account requirement.

Native/vendor baseline: installed-client help could not be executed in this web-only lane. [Codex source at rust-v0.160.1](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.160.1/codex-rs/cli/src/main.rs) exposes app-server daemon management, exec-server and remote-control surfaces; [Claude Code's changelog through 2.1.292](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) documents background commands and their lifecycle fixes. These were considered native candidates, but the examined sources do not establish acceptance as hosts for this application/database workload. This is not an installed-client capability-absence claim. Recent-push organization API listings were attempted for Microsoft, FastAPI, Vercel and Caddyserver but were inaccessible through web fetch; a complete vendor-organization census remains pending. Repository APIs and official vendor deployment guidance supplied the verified baseline. Scoped ai-memory was not exposed.

Winner health: [FastAPI metadata](https://api.github.com/repos/fastapi/fastapi), [Next.js metadata](https://api.github.com/repos/vercel/next.js) and [PostgreSQL metadata](https://api.github.com/repos/postgres/postgres) show unchanged canonical names and unarchived repositories. Their default-branch commit queries each returned activity on 2026-10-06: [FastAPI](https://api.github.com/repos/fastapi/fastapi/commits?since=2026-07-08T00:00:00Z&per_page=1), [Next.js](https://api.github.com/repos/vercel/next.js/commits?since=2026-07-08T00:00:00Z&per_page=1), [PostgreSQL](https://api.github.com/repos/postgres/postgres/commits?since=2026-07-08T00:00:00Z&per_page=1). [FastAPI 0.142.2](https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/releases/tag/0.142.2) fixes startup when automatic OpenTelemetry configuration fails; the supplied installed pin remains 0.141.1. [Next.js v16.3.8](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/releases/tag/v16.3.8) contains security fixes, including self-hosted cache-poisoning fixes; components_vs_upstream already records that installed version, so the sealed winner's 16.3.5 is not treated as the current installation. [PostgreSQL's official release archive](https://www.postgresql.org/about/newsarchive/pgsql/) identifies 18.6 on 2026-08-13 and 19 Beta 4 on 2026-09-24; a missing GitHub latest-release value is not evidence of stale maintenance. Current API licenses are MIT, MIT and NOASSERTION respectively; no license-history audit was performed and license did not affect ranking.

Comparative standing: native_proven supports fixture operation, not measured best hosting. The [October layer review](https://github.com/seathatflowsinourveins/native-agent-stack/blob/main/evidence/artifacts/new-wsl-layer-reviews-20261001/hosting-services.json) and examined receipts leave current-pin browser acceptance, independent-host recovery and matched full-stack deployment evidence incomplete. proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: Preregister the trial with the same native account and next_action's frozen task, account and effect checks. Run it on WSL and on one macos-arm64 Mac, which is untested. Arms: the stack pin 2.1.284 against 2.1.291 or later (installed 2.1.292; skip 2.1.288 to 2.1.290), N>=5 per arm. Each trial starts a `claude --bg` session and a `claude -p --output-format stream-json` session, with a turn that issues a parallel tool batch including one MCP call. Kill the session with SIGKILL mid-turn, then resume it by id (`claude --resume <id>`, or `claude respawn` for --bg). Measure four things: the share of pre-kill turns present after resume, MCP call success after resume, duplicated or re-sent turns, and whether new assistant or usage entries reach the transcript after `claude stop <id>`. Move the pin only if the newer build keeps every pre-kill turn in every trial where 2.1.284 loses any, with no regression on the frozen checks. Otherwise keep 2.1.284 and record the outcome against gap 4. Any task-quality arm runs under Harbor or Inspect.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: FIRST-PARTY SURFACE OF THE WINNER, not a replacement. It covers the native app-server, its shared local daemon and the in-repo Python and TypeScript SDKs, all used through the existing ChatGPT sign-in. Gap 0's only receipt (gap-wave2 codex-resume-pinned-build.json) is N=1 on 0.155.1 and states that a later release needs its own trial. The stack now installs 0.160.0 and this host runs 0.160.1, where local sessions moved to paginated thread history (`codex migrate-rollouts`: 'Inspect or migrate legacy local sessions to paginated thread history'; rust-v0.159.0 #48151 item anchors for thread/items/list). Resuming a 0.155.1-era session on the current pin is therefore unqualified. open_gaps[4] has no follow-up. `codex exec --help` (0.160.1) lists only the resume, fork and review subcommands plus --json JSONL events, with no turn-interrupt or steer control, so cancellation there is a process signal. The vendor Python SDK `openai-codex` (sdk/python) reuses the existing Codex authentication, ChatGPT login included. It exposes per-turn stream(), steer() and interrupt(), thread_resume and thread_fork, and thread_list with cursors. The shared daemon (`codex app-server daemon`, `codex agents`) is a native session manager. The same SDK path is the agent-sdks layer's winner (component codex at 0.155.1), whose open gaps record no native cancel receipt and no multi-turn resume, so one preregistered trial feeds both layers. rust-v0.160.0 adds #49105 (unsent queued messages resume after reconnection without duplicate sends) and #49160 (saved permissions restored on resume). #49144, #49161 and #49171 fix TUI provider, reasoning-summary and verbosity settings, and which sessions the resume and fork history lists. They are not crash-durability fixes, contrary to the seed's grouping.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: Preregister the trial with the same ChatGPT sign-in and next_action's frozen task, account and effect checks. Run it on WSL first, then on one macos-arm64 Mac, N>=5 per check. Check 1: resume a 0.155.1-era session on 0.160.1, before and after `codex migrate-rollouts`. It passes with the same thread id, every pre-upgrade turn returned by thread/items/list, and no lost turns. Check 2: SIGKILL the app-server daemon mid-turn, restart it, then thread_resume the same id. It passes when pre-kill items are retained and a queued message is delivered exactly once (#49105). Check 3: cancel a running turn with the SDK's interrupt() and, for comparison, SIGINT and SIGKILL of `codex exec --json`, with both arms on the same Codex build (the SDK pins openai-codex-cli-bin 0.153.4 by default). Measure seconds until events stop, and confirm that no further item or usage events follow the stop. Adopt the SDK/app-server path as this layer's programmatic surface only if it passes every check `codex exec --json` passes and also passes one of the cancellation or recovery checks that exec fails. Otherwise keep exec --json and record the results against gaps 0 and 4. Any task-quality arm runs under Harbor or Inspect.

proposed.demonstrated_gap:
The requirement asks for verification of the changed behavior. No lane records whether the lines a change touched were run by any check.

CI runs the whole suite (`python3 -m unittest -v --durations 50`, .github/workflows/validate.yml:239), but no workflow measures code coverage. The workflows that mention 'coverage' mean other things: catalog coverage joins (validate.yml:114), workflow-security coverage (adoption-bootstrap.yml:211) or lockfile coverage (security-scan.yml:76-77). The repository root has no .coveragerc or pyproject.toml.

The vendor baseline does not cover this:
- The Claude Code CHANGELOG through 2.1.292 mentions 'coverage' once, about Admin API coverage in /claude-api.
- The installed codex-cli 0.160.1 `--help`, `review --help` and `exec --help` never mention it.
- `/code-review` and `codex review` give model judgments of a diff, not execution evidence.

The gap2 mutation-catch receipt states its own limit: one mutation per tool, and it 'does not measure mutation-detection rates'.

diff-cover turns coverage.py data plus a git diff into a per-change report (HTML/JSON/Markdown) that lists the uncovered changed lines and exits non-zero under `--fail-under`. That is deterministic, change-scoped evidence that keeps the failure. It also serves the north star's paper-lane tests.

Feasibility risk:
- Of the 266 .py files in tests/, 83 spawn child processes through sys.executable, 7 pass a bare "python3" without sys.executable, and 8 pass -I.
- The coverage.py docs (page labelled 7.16.2) document `patch = subprocess` with `parallel` and `coverage combine` for children started by subprocess, os.system, execv or spawnv.
- Children started through a bare python3 found on PATH may run an interpreter that lacks coverage, and would then go unmeasured.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn:
Preregister a bounded trial on the workstation. Keep the repository read-only and write all outputs outside the checkout.

Setup: run the unchanged unittest suite under coverage.py with `patch = subprocess` and `parallel = true`, then `coverage combine`, `coverage xml`, and `diff-cover coverage.xml --compare-branch=<base> --format json:...,markdown:...`. Apply it to three recent merged PRs (#703, #744, #730), to the gap2 app mutation, and to a sample of the tests/canary_mutants.py fault classes applied as diffs.

Gate 1 (feasibility): choose modules that only child processes reach, such as the canary two-process design. After combine they must show measured lines above zero; otherwise relabel to keep_but_compare.

Gate 2 (discrimination): surviving (unkilled) injected faults must fall on lines diff-cover reports as uncovered at a higher rate than killed faults do, and every uncovered changed line must be kept in the JSON/Markdown report.

Do not adopt if the covered/uncovered split carries no information about kill versus survive on that set, or if full-suite wall-clock under coverage exceeds a preregistered bound, for example 2x the plain run.

proposed.demonstrated_gap:
This is a review harness, not a competitor to a winner. It targets open_gaps[1]: no PR review result is recorded for any candidate. It also fills a gap in the P3 seeded-defect review comparison (docs/decisions/2026-10-02-github-automation-practice.md:61-71), which names no corpus or harness and would end in a self-built runner.

What the upstream provides:
- License MIT; created 2026-02-06; 48 default-branch commits since 2026-07-08; head e616e84 (2026-08-30).
- A fixed offline set of 50 PRs from Sentry, Grafana, Cal.com, Discourse and Keycloak, with 173 human-verified golden comments.
- An open pipeline: fork, download, LLM extract, dedup, judge.
- Published results for each judge.

Gateway fit: the extract, dedup and judge steps use the OpenAI Python SDK (AsyncOpenAI), with a provider-prefixed model id read from MARTIAN_MODEL (default openai/gpt-4o-mini). The judge therefore speaks the gateway's OpenAI-compatible protocol, although the base-URL source and model-id mapping are unverified.

What the published results contain:
- I derived figures from offline/results/openai_gpt-5.2/evaluations.json at e616e84 (GPT-5.2 judge, all categories, micro-averaged). These are my own numbers, not Martian's profile and F-beta scoring.
- The claude-code key scores P 0.423, R 0.410, F1 0.416. A separate claude key scores F1 0.393. The tool and model versions behind either key are not documented in what I read.
- No key exists for Codex, PR-Agent or PR-AF.
- The published judges are older models (Opus 4.5, Sonnet 4.5, GPT-5.2).
- Neither current native review path is measured: Claude Code 2.1.292 /code-review and codex review 0.160.1.

Limitation stated by the upstream: the PRs are static and public, so they may appear in training data.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn:
The decision run uses one current judge model through the gateway (MARTIAN_MODEL) for every arm. Published judges are not reused, so no stale model is needed.
- Re-run extract, dedup and judge on the published claude-code reviews in results/benchmark_data.json.
- Run the same steps on two new arms. Their reviews come from forks of the 50 PRs in a separate scratch org, so this repository's pull-requests:write rule is untouched:
  - Claude Code 2.1.292 `/code-review --comment`;
  - `codex review --base` 0.160.1, posted as a PR comment.
- Compare precision, recall and F-beta for each arm.
- Optional sanity check, only if an original judge is routable: reproduce the published claude-code evaluations under that judge.

The harness is overturned in either of two cases:
- the gateway cannot serve the pipeline's OpenAI-SDK calls without new vendor keys;
- the planned self-built seeded-defect corpus separates the arms where this one does not, at equal cost.

What it is:
- An agent-aware Git layer, the class the critic flagged.
- It installs hooks for Claude Code (.claude/settings.json) and Codex (.codex/hooks.json), among other agents.
- It tracks sessions independently in each git worktree and indexes checkpoints with commits.

It does not create or own worktrees, review PRs or produce structural diffs. Its addition is session provenance, which this requirement does not name. git-ai, already judged, covers that class.

Decisive reason: per its README, transcripts are stored in per-checkpoint git refs that ride along with pushes to one elected remote, and 'If your repository is public, this data is visible to anyone'. Redaction is best-effort. This repository is public, and AGENTS.md forbids raw conversations in records.

Not verified: operation against a private checkpoint remote only, and operation without an account (the README documents `entire login`).

output.notes:
Scope: reproducible Git ownership and review of US-equities research, historical-simulation and adapter changes. No installations, candidate execution, credential reads, publications or host trials were performed. Comparisons are proposed, not measured results. Stars and licenses did not determine ranking.

Native controls: installed help could not be inspected in this web-only lane. Source at rust-v0.160.1 confirms Codex review, apply and worktree support for new sessions; code review itself rejects --worktree. The patch release concerns Windows remote-MCP environment preservation, not demonstrated improvement for this layer. Claude's changelog through 2.1.292 confirms native worktree workflows, /diff, /code-review with finding-count controls, and /ultrareview; the latter uploads local changes and needs separate privacy qualification. These native surfaces remain comparison controls, without re-proposing already-judged openai/codex or anthropics/claude-code. [Claude changelog](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

Its release improves pathological diff performance, but no matched structural-diff comparison was established here. proposed.demonstrated_gap: This is a vendor-native surface. It is installed at 2.1.292 but the stack does not use it. It covers the layer's open gaps 0 and 1, which the three winners (all local_integration, no measured gain) leave open, and it adds an indicator of whether a skill fired. (a) Measurement: `claude plugin eval` (added in 2.1.269) runs a plugin or skills-dir eval suite. With `--ablation with-without` it adds a no-plugin baseline arm and reports the score delta. It runs each case 3 times by default, supports free and LLM graders and a cost ceiling, and writes JSON and HTML reports. Under with-without, a `tool_used: Skill` grader becomes a with-only 'plugin-fired indicator'. That shows whether the skill fired in the top-level run; it does not test what a worker sees listed. The stack has no retained skill-arm fixture today. (b) Single-source instructions: the documented 'Project instructions' value `claude-md-and-agents-md` loads each directory's CLAUDE.md and then its AGENTS.md, and skips an AGENTS.md that is already imported. The value is stored as pluginConfigs["cc-plugin-agents-md@builtin"].options.instructionFiles and is read only from user, --settings or managed settings, never from project or local settings. The ID was agents-md@builtin before 2.1.285, so the stack's 2.1.284 pin uses the old ID. The stack keeps four hand-written `@AGENTS.md` shims (root, adoption/scaffold, blueprints/us-equities, blueprints/convergence-practice/application-delivery), and its settings template sets no such key. (c) Task-scoped activation for stack-authored rules and skills: `.claude/rules/*.md` and SKILL.md `paths:` load only for matching files, and since 2.1.288 they also load on Write and Edit. `/doctor prompt-audit` (2.1.283) reports stale paths and contradicting instruction files. The repo has no .claude/rules, and no installed skill uses `paths:`. Limits: `paths:` lives in each SKILL.md, so applying it to third-party packs would mean editing upstream files (a fork), and skillOverrides has no path option. The claim therefore covers stack-authored rules and skills only. Pin drift: the stack pins 2.1.284 while the host runs 2.1.292, and loading rules on Write and Edit needs 2.1.288. The 2.1.282 and 2.1.284 fixes are both inside the 2.1.284 pin. They stop repository, user, --add-dir, marketplace, claude.ai and npm skills or plugins from pre-approving their own tools via allowed-tools under allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly. Trial constraints: (1) Pass --no-publish, because the HTML report goes to claude.ai by default. (2) Pass an explicit --judge-model, because the default is haiku. (3) Run plugin eval against a scratch plugin directory that wraps a copy of each skill. Cases and results are written below the target directory and would change skill trees whose hashes the vercel lock records. (4) Set the instruction mode through a per-launch --settings file, because a ~/.claude/settings.json entry changes instruction loading for every project on the host. Unverified: whether a bare ~/.claude/skills/<name> directory resolves as a target (the help says installed and skills-dir plugins both resolve).
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: Use one frozen case set of at least 8 cases from this repo's lifecycle tasks, covering 3 installed winner skills (for example search-first, tdd and codeql), on the same model. Run it through both harnesses. (1) skill-creator's paired benchmark: with_skill and without_skill arms spawned in the same turn, assertions graded to grading.json, and aggregate_benchmark reporting pass_rate mean and stddev plus tokens and time. (2) `claude plugin eval <scratch plugin dir wrapping copies of the skills> --ablation with-without --runs 3 --no-publish --judge-model <opus id> --json`. The native harness becomes the retained skill-arm measurement only if every non-flaky case's with/without delta has the same sign in both harnesses and its per-case variance is no higher. Otherwise skill-creator stays the mandated harness. Separately, set `claude-md-and-agents-md` through a per-launch --settings file. It retires the four @AGENTS.md shims only if, with the shims removed, the /context instruction rows and InstructionsLoaded hook records show the same files loaded exactly once each, at the root and in each of the three subdirectories.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: APM is a cross-client manifest and lockfile for the skills and instruction files this stack installs and records by hand. One apm.yml declares skills, instructions, agents, hooks, plugins and MCP servers. `apm install` deploys to Claude: skills to .claude/skills and instructions to .claude/rules/<name>.md, and the CLAUDE.md compile leaves out rules that are already deployed. It also deploys to Codex: .agents/skills plus .codex. The codex target has no instructions primitive and needs a separate root-context compile to AGENTS.md. apm.lock records resolved sources and content hashes. Every install scans for hidden Unicode. `apm audit` rebuilds the context in scratch and diffs it against the tree. It also exports an SBOM, and the README offers a drop-in replacement for `npx skills add`. The stack today runs vercel-labs/skills 1.7.0 global installs plus a hand-kept adoption/skills/manifest.json (pins, hashes, exclusions). That is glue an upstream now provides. APM does not decide what loads per task (the native client surfaces do that). Claude Code's native claude-md-and-agents-md mode also removes most of its instruction-sync value for these two clients. It is therefore a comparison against dyoshikawa/rulesync (keep_but_compare, 2026-10-06) and the vercel CLI, not a trial against the winners now. Unknown: whether the claude target maps package applyTo globs to `paths:`. The retrieved targets matrix documents that mapping only for antigravity. Supply-chain facts: 3 published repository advisories, all from May 2026: GHSA-xhrw-5qxx-jpwr (high: plugin.json component paths escape the plugin root during install), GHSA-q5pp-gvjg-h7v4 (high: symlinks are dereferenced during install) and GHSA-mq5j-pw29-jcv3 (medium: Windows tar path overwrite). Fixed versions were not checked here. Maintenance: v0.33.0 on 2026-10-02 and a default-branch commit on 2026-10-06.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: In a throwaway HOME and worktree on each host, declare the manifest's pinned skills (adoption/skills/manifest.json sources at their recorded refs) in apm.yml and run `apm install` for the claude and codex targets. Promote APM to targeted only if all five checks pass: (1) every installed skill tree's git tree SHA equals the vercel lock's skillFolderHash for the same ref; (2) /skills and the Codex listing show the same skills, with the description-char totals unchanged (9,484 for Claude and 9,165 for Codex in the manifest budget); (3) `apm audit` flags a planted hand-edit and a planted hidden-Unicode SKILL.md that the current path does not flag; (4) a second clean host reproduces byte-identical trees from apm.yml and apm.lock alone; (5) nothing is written outside the declared target directories. Any tree mismatch, listing change or stray write keeps the vercel CLI plus the hand manifest.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: Same maintainer as the stale alternative alphalens-reloaded: Stefan Jansen, pm@ml4trading.io, in both pyproject files. This repository fills two gaps the winners leave open. (1) Open gap 1: skfolio 1.4.12 WalkForward exposes only purged_size (default 0) and has no embargo parameter, so development labels can cross fold boundaries. ml4t-diagnostic ships purged walk-forward, combinatorial/CPCV and calendar-aware splitters (splitters/walk_forward.py, combinatorial.py, cpcv, calendar.py, group_isolation.py). (2) Strategy qualification has no selection-bias correction. skfolio has no Deflated Sharpe Ratio or PBO (code search for 'deflated' returns 0), yet the retained broad-universe study tested 15 signal variants. ml4t-diagnostic implements DSR (evaluation/stats/deflated_sharpe_ratio.py), PBO, RAS, FDR control and White's Reality Check, plus HAC-adjusted IC that replaces alphalens-style factor evaluation. Caveats: it is pre-1.0 (0.1.8) despite a 'Production/Stable' classifier. Its CHANGELOG lags the releases (last entry 0.1.2, 2026-08-17). Correctness on our inputs is unmeasured. It does not close the point-in-time-universe or total-return-label gaps. macOS is untested.

Pass means zero overlaps while the receipt's test windows are preserved. (b) Selection bias: DSR with the true trial count, and PBO via CSCV, must match the Bailey and Lopez de Prado (2014) closed forms and an independent implementation (RiskLabAI 3.2.0; arch SPA/StepM as a reality-check cross-check) within a preregistered tolerance on identical estimator choices. Adopt it as the layer's strategy-qualification component beside skfolio if both checks pass. This unit serves causal US-equity research and reproducible historical simulation before independently qualified paper trading. No installations, candidate execution, credential inspection or live-trading actions occurred. All research limits were reached; counts include failed requests, skill-source reads and receipt reads. GitHub API requests are counted separately from ordinary page fetches.

Native baseline: inspected [Codex 0.160.1 CLI source](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.160.1/codex-rs/cli/src/main.rs), its [release changelog](https://github.com/openai/codex/releases/tag/rust-v0.160.1), and the [Claude Code changelog section for 2.1.292](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md). HTML fallbacks were incomplete or stale, and the filtered Microsoft retry failed. Candidate-specific official repository APIs, releases and source files succeeded. Both have retained integration evidence, but their standing as best for PIT US-equity research lacks a retained comparative quality result; incumbency is not that evidence.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: All three winners are 'untested' on macos-arm64, and the accepted CUDA vLLM service cannot use the Apple GPU. vllm-metal is the vLLM organization's own Apple Silicon plugin. Compared with SocratiCode's documented macOS path (native Ollama for Metal, README v1.16.0 line 135), it adds server parity with WSL: the same `vllm serve --runner pooling --convert embed` flags used in the stack's benchmark receipt, and the same OpenAI-compatible API that SocratiCode reaches through EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=lmstudio. It does not close the cross-host gap. Its pooling support is declared 'experimental text-only', and its pooling table lists only Qwen3-Embedding, Qwen3-Reranker, BGE-M3 and multilingual-e5-base. It does not list the incumbent Nemotron-3-Embed (model_type ministral3) or EmbeddingGemma 2. A Mac index would therefore need a different embedder, and a WSL Qdrant snapshot could not be queried on the Mac (open gap 2). It is labelled keep_but_compare, not targeted, because llama.cpp offers the same-model path and vllm-metal adds only packaging parity.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: Re-run when docs/supported_models.md adds ministral3 or EmbeddingGemma 2 to the pooling table, or when pooling leaves 'experimental'. Step 1 is an embedding-parity gate: embed a fixed sample (the 35 sealed queries plus 200 corpus chunks) and compare it with the reference implementation's vectors against a cosine threshold set before the run (for example a mean of at least 0.99). Step 2 runs only if step 1 passes: the sealed 35-question set through SocratiCode on the Mac, against llama.cpp and native-Ollama arms. Score by line overlap at top-5 with a paired per-question test, where 'within one question' means 2.9 points of the best arm. Also record p50/p95 latency, full-index wall time, peak RSS and a kill-restart re-index.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: This is Hugging Face's own embedding server. Compared with SocratiCode's macOS default (native Ollama) and with vllm-metal, it adds four things. First, a Metal path that is not marked experimental: the README says 'Metal support for local execution on Macs' and offers a prebuilt Homebrew binary for M1, M2, M3 and M4. M5 is not listed, which is a platform-fit fact, not a blocker. Second, it serves safetensors weights with no GGUF conversion. Third, there is an Ada Lovelace image (ghcr.io/huggingface/text-embeddings-inference:89-1.9) for the RTX 4090. Fourth, its OpenAI-compatible endpoints can be consumed by SocratiCode's lmstudio provider. Supported architectures: Nomic, BERT, CamemBERT, XLM-RoBERTa, JinaBERT, Mistral, GTE, Qwen2, MPNet, ModernBERT, Qwen3 and Gemma3. The README lists Mistral but not ministral3. Whether TEI accepts the incumbent Nemotron-3-Embed config and reproduces its bidirectional attention is unverified, not refuted. EmbeddingGemma 2, which is based on Gemma 4, is not listed. Maintenance facts: 14 default-branch commits since 2026-07-08, and v1.9.4 (2026-09-15) was the first release after v1.9.3 (2026-03-23).

proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: Step 1, parity gate: on WSL (CUDA) and the Mac (Metal), embed the 35 sealed queries plus 200 fixed corpus chunks through llama-server with a locally converted Nemotron-3-Embed-1B GGUF. Compare the vectors with vLLM 0.25.0's for the same inputs, and fail the arm below a cosine threshold set before the run (for example a mean of at least 0.99). Step 2 runs only if parity passes: restore a WSL Qdrant snapshot on the Mac and score the sealed 35-question set through SocratiCode. It passes if Recall@5 and MRR are within one question (2.9 points) of WSL's 0.971 and 0.853. Step 3 adds an EmbeddingGemma 2 arm: the ggml-org GGUF at Q8_0 and BF16, parity-gated against the card's sentence-transformers vectors, run against Nemotron. Use the sealed set plus an identifier-free paraphrase subset that must be written and sealed before any run, and a paired per-question test. Native Ollama is the macOS control arm. Adopt llama.cpp for the Mac if steps 1 and 2 pass. Switch the model only if EmbeddingGemma 2 is not worse on that test and uses less VRAM and time. If it wins, then compare llama.cpp with a vLLM build pinned at bb87d227d4, or the first release containing embedding_gemma2.py.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: Measured against SocratiCode and the Qdrant vendor baseline, whose MCP has no code indexer. codanna needs no Docker, no Qdrant and no embedding service. The index lives on disk under .codanna/. A roughly 150 MB embedding model downloads once and runs in-process (fastembed, per src/semantic and src/vector/embedding.rs). `serve --watch` keeps the index current, and it installs on macOS through Homebrew. That gives a one-directory recoverable state for restic and a macOS path where all winners are untested. Gaps: there is no published retrieval-quality benchmark (the README gives only speed, about 3 ms per semantic lookup). Its default model is in the size class that lost in the stack's own benchmark (bge-small-en-v1.5, 512 tokens: Recall@5 0.771 against 0.971). Symbol-level indexing may miss prose and config spans. The default model's identity and context length were not verified.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: First write and seal an identifier-free paraphrase subset. Then run codanna (default model) against SocratiCode 1.16.0 with Nemotron-3-Embed-1B on the sealed 35-question set and that subset, scoring line overlap at top-5 with a paired per-question test. Add a restart drill that kills indexing mid-run with SIGKILL, and compare a restic restore of .codanna/ on another host with a Qdrant snapshot restore. It overturns the winner only if its recall is within one question of SocratiCode and both lifecycle drills pass.

output.notes:
North-star action: improve source-grounded investigation of historical simulation code and the separate IBKR/Alpaca adapters, with LEAN as comparison; no trading, installation or candidate execution occurred.

Correction to the sealed gap text: a held-out comparison does exist. The [September receipt](https://github.com/seathatflowsinourveins/native-agent-stack/blob/main/evidence/artifacts/gap-wave2-20260923/semantic-rag/held-out-recall-benchmark.json) records Nemotron Recall@5 34/35 and MRR 0.853 versus BGE-small 27/35 and 0.592. However, chunk losses differed substantially and many questions named exact identifiers. It also records a successful isolated vLLM 0.30.0 BGE service, so '0.30.0 untested' is too broad. This does not qualify every model on that version. The watcher receipt was reachable but its body was not returned within the browser output; its supplied 'advanced' status is retained without claiming full recovery qualification.

Winner standing: the checked receipt supports the Nemotron model on one limited corpus. It does not establish SocratiCode as the best indexer, Qdrant as the best store or vLLM as the best embedding service. Those comparative rankings remain retained-control decisions rather than measured wins on the target equities projects.

Winner health: current [SocratiCode metadata](https://api.github.com/repos/giancarloerra/SocratiCode), [Qdrant metadata](https://api.github.com/repos/qdrant/qdrant) and [vLLM metadata](https://api.github.com/repos/vllm-project/vllm) remain unarchived, with names and licenses matching the supplied baseline. [SocratiCode v1.16.0](https://github.com/giancarloerra/SocratiCode/releases/tag/v1.16.0) adds Git-triggered refresh and startup/deletion recovery fixes. [Qdrant v1.19.2](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/releases/tag/v1.19.2) fixes restart persistence, torn writes and search correctness; this upgrade deserves recovery qualification before replacing the store. [vLLM v0.31.0](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/releases/tag/v0.31.0) includes pooling padding/normalization fixes and experimental engine snapshots; neither establishes whole-stack recovery. Winner default-branch 90-day activity was not separately queried; pushed_at was not used as a substitute.

Include this as a second native control. Installed Codex --help and installed Claude capabilities could not be inspected, so native semantic-index absence is not asserted.

Model seed: [Google's EmbeddingGemma 2 card](https://huggingface.co/google/embeddinggemma-2), retrieved through search, describes approximately 740M total parameters, a selectable 270M text-only configuration, 8K context, code-specific prefixes and a claimed code-task improvement over its predecessor. The precise seeded 744M count and September 14 release date were not independently verified. This is a worthwhile model comparison lead, not proof of superiority over Nemotron or compatibility with the proposed servers. No corresponding canonical GitHub model repository was verified. Google, Qwen, jinaai and Salesforce createdAt-sorted Hub API passes were attempted but inaccessible; current-model inventory coverage is incomplete. Jina's vendor-published code GGUF supplies a verified model option for the llama.cpp comparison.

No qualifying new evidence was established within budget for cocoindex-io/cocoindex-code, colbymchenry/codegraph, FlagOpen/FlagEmbedding, lightonai/next-plaid, lightonai/pylate, ollama/ollama, OSU-NLP-Group/HippoRAG, yoanbernabeu/grepai, zhangfw123/core-bench-eval or zilliztech/claude-context; these remain un-reopened, not newly refuted. Coverage and completeness critic: the four pushed-sorted organization API requests failed; vendor-scoped repository search provided partial fallback, not a complete organization inventory. All proposed repositories have a positive default-branch commit result after July 8. Full dependency/advisory audits were not performed. Next sweep should complete vendor inventories, especially NVIDIA's incumbent-model family, and compare code-specialized models, rerankers and late-interaction approaches. Destination-hardware measurements, independent physical-host restore and native-client rebinding remain necessary. Freeze independently reviewed conceptual questions before comparisons and use upstream evaluation/performance harnesses; no custom runner was created.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: The layer has no consumer for the reranker-model slot's 'second stage of local retrieval'. SocratiCode, the code-retrieval winner, has no rerank stage or hook. At 1e829bf7ddf1 its README documents only dense + BM25 search fused by RRF (lines 52, 560, 632, 702, 1228), and the word 'rerank' appears only in general prose (line 1698). Release notes v1.13.3 through v1.16.0 never mention reranking. A search of its issues for 'rerank' returns only #63, a hybrid-prefetch refactor. ChunkHound is the maintained upstream integration point that was found, so no glue is needed. At 092792a93660 it defines embedding.rerank_model, rerank_url, rerank_format (cohere, tei or auto) and rerank_batch_size (configuration.md:386-390). When the provider supports reranking, its semantic search switches to 'Multi-hop + reranking' (search_service.py:72,116-118). Its docs name vLLM as the drop-in reranker server (configuration.md:828-830). It can therefore call the Cohere-compatible /rerank endpoint of the vLLM winner directly (vLLM v0.31.0 scoring.md:22-23). Its code_research tool can use the Claude Code CLI or Codex CLI as the LLM with no key, so it runs on native accounts (README:59-60,155). The cost is that it would replace SocratiCode and Qdrant rather than compose with them. It stores data in DuckDB (the stable default) or LanceDB (experimental) (configuration.md:401-402). The only restore evidence established so far, Qdrant snapshots, therefore does not carry over.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: The comparison runs at pipeline level, on the layer's frozen set of target-project questions with expected source spans (GAP0). Every arm uses the same embedder served by vLLM: nvidia/Nemotron-3-Embed-1B-BF16, the model in evidence/receipts/native-rag.json. Arms: (a) SocratiCode 1.16.0 with dense + BM25 RRF; (b) ChunkHound without rerank_model, which runs single-hop; (c) ChunkHound with rerank_format set explicitly to cohere and rerank_url pointing at a vLLM /rerank instance serving Qwen/Qwen3-Reranker-4B. That model is loaded with the hf_overrides from vLLM scoring.md:85-88. Do not use ChunkHound's documented example, 'vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B --task score' (configuration.md:830). It omits those overrides and picks the size that regressed on MTEB-Code. Arm (d) holds two controls: the slot finalist llama-nemotron-rerank-1b-v2 and the generic bge-reranker-v2-m3. Measure paired Recall@5 and nDCG@5 against the expected spans, plus the added p50 and p95 latency per query. Pin --gpu-memory-utilization for each vLLM instance and report each model's weights plus its configured KV cache. The default reservation of about 90% would otherwise mask the real footprint. The embedder and the local generation model stay resident on the 24 GB RTX 4090 throughout. Index and watcher kill-restart recovery and DuckDB restore form an explicit cost arm. ChunkHound is refuted if arm (c) does not beat arms (a) and (b) on top-5 by a margin set before the run, or if recovery and restore cannot be re-established. SocratiCode is overturned if arm (c) wins within the latency and memory budget and recovery passes.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: The reranker-model slot seeded Qwen3-Reranker (slots.json), but the order-2 packet never gave it a disposition. It is absent from selection (C08 llama-nemotron-rerank-1b-v2, C03 bge-reranker-v2-gemma), from not_selected (C01, C02, C05, C06, C07) and from excluded (C04). The finalists' recorded evidence is general-domain: a BEIR average for bge-reranker-v2-gemma and a Recall@5 gain for the Nemotron model. Neither has code evidence on record. Published code evidence shows that off-the-shelf cross-encoders hurt code retrieval. Qwen reranked the top-100 Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B candidates on MTEB-Code, where the first stage scores 75.41. On that run, BGE-reranker-v2-m3, the slot's named smaller alternative, scores 41.38. jina-multilingual-reranker-v2-base scores 58.98, gte-multilingual-reranker-base 54.18 and Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B 73.42. Qwen3-Reranker-4B scores 81.20 and the 8B model 81.22 (card lines 267-279). These are the vendor's own runs and have been on the card since 2025. They are not new upstream evidence, but they are evidence the slot never weighed. Two independent results agree. Octocode's 127-query code benchmark shows bge-reranker-base cutting Hit@5 from 0.732 to 0.598. CoREB (arXiv 2605.04615) finds no off-the-shelf reranker that is net-positive across its three code tasks. Serving fits the winner. The card requires vllm>=0.8.5 (line 174), and vLLM v0.31.0 scoring.md:52,85-88 loads the model with hf_overrides, so the accepted 0.25.0 pin can serve it. ChunkHound and codeseek both document Qwen3 rerankers. The installed QMD already ships qwen3-reranker-0.6b-q8_0 for docs (QMD README:582-587), which is the size that regressed on code.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: Model level: run MTEB 2.22.5 two-stage evaluation on MTEB(code, v1). Its retrieval.py accepts a CrossEncoderProtocol model over top_ranked candidate lists (lines 19-21, 395-396, 497-536), so no self-written runner is needed. Whether MTEB already has a Qwen3-Reranker implementation was not verified. Take the same top-100 lists from the embedder in use, nvidia/Nemotron-3-Embed-1B-BF16, and rerank them six ways: none, Qwen3-Reranker-4B, Qwen3-Reranker-8B, llama-nemotron-rerank-1b-v2, bge-reranker-v2-gemma and bge-reranker-v2-m3. Report paired nDCG@10 and Recall@5 deltas. Pipeline level: add Qwen3-Reranker-4B as an arm of the slot's own deciding comparison. That comparison uses frozen code, docs and session sets, nDCG@5 and Recall@5, and the added p50 and p95 latency. Pin --gpu-memory-utilization for each vLLM instance and report weights plus configured KV cache, not the default reservation. On the 24 GB RTX 4090 the binding constraint is about 8 GB of BF16 weights (an estimate) alongside the embedder and the generation model. The model is refuted for the code stratum if it does not improve top-5 over the first stage alone, or if it cannot fit alongside the resident models. In that case select no reranker for code (C01) or one of the finalists. If the Qwen3-VL-Reranker-2B and 8B cards (both 2026-01-07) report MTEB-Code, add them as arms.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: Octocode ships the only reproducible code-retrieval ablation found with line-range ground truth. It runs 127 code queries against a pinned corpus, octocode@b1771ba (README:107; RESULTS.md:3-5). In that ablation, keyword-tilted RRF (0.3/0.7) raises Hit@5 from 0.598 to 0.732 and Recall@10 from 0.671 to 0.807 over dense-only and default RRF. A generic local cross-encoder, fastembed:bge-reranker-base, cuts Hit@5 from 0.732 to 0.598 (RESULTS.md:13-20; README:112-117). This bears on GAP0. It also raises the question of whether SocratiCode's RRF, which documents no weight option, leaves code-retrieval quality on the table. Octocode combines semantic search, BM25 and reranking behind an MCP server (README:88-89). It has limits at 839702ccb71c. Its local embedding and rerank paths run in-process through FastEmbed or HuggingFace (API_KEYS.md:84-110). OpenAI-compatible endpoints are documented only for the LLM, through 'local:' chat completions (API_KEYS.md:216-248). No external embedding or rerank endpoint was found, so it cannot use the embedder or reranker served by vLLM. Its code-aware reranker path is cloud Voyage, which needs credentials.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: Run octocode's hybrid_30_70 configuration (local FastEmbed, no reranker) on the frozen target-project question set. Compare it with SocratiCode 1.16.0 and with ChunkHound plus a vLLM-served Qwen3-Reranker-4B on Recall@5, nDCG@5, latency and index recovery. Promote it to targeted_candidate if its local arm beats both, or if it adds an OpenAI-compatible embedding or rerank provider. Its own benchmark/run_matrix.py evaluates only octocode, so it is a reference result rather than a cross-tool harness.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: codeseek is a second code-retrieval MCP that registers with Claude Code and Codex (README:24,122-126). It combines LanceDB dense search, Tantivy BM25 and RRF, then reranks with a cross-encoder through a configurable /v1/rerank endpoint (README:190-217, 250-275). Its documented reranker is Qwen/Qwen3-Reranker-4B (README:214,268,285), the size with published MTEB-Code gains. That makes it a fallback integration point if ChunkHound fails. Its documented endpoints are SiliconFlow cloud, and compatibility with vLLM's Cohere/Jina-style /v1/rerank is not verified. A maintenance fact, not an exclusion: the newest default-branch commit is 981bd23800d1, from 2026-07-30, inside the 90-day window. The repository was created 2026-06-03.

Point its embedding and reranker api_base_url at vLLM. Keep it only if it beats both ChunkHound with reranking and SocratiCode, and its maintenance continues.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: fastembed is the vendor-official library from the org of the Qdrant winner. v0.8.1 (2026-09-22) ships ONNX CPU inference plus an optional fastembed-gpu package (README:9-24). It also ships TextCrossEncoder rerankers (README:178-188), ColBERT late interaction (117-123) and SPLADE/BM42 (85-111). Two reasons are decisive for this requirement. (1) It is a Python library with no HTTP surface. Reaching SocratiCode, which has no rerank hook, or ChunkHound's rerank_url would need self-written glue. The Qdrant-native ColBERT multistage route would need SocratiCode to write multivectors, which it does not. (2) Its shipped cross-encoders are the generic class that regressed code retrieval in two independent measurements. The catalog (onnx_text_cross_encoder.py:18-75) holds ms-marco MiniLM L-6/L-12, bge-reranker-base, bge-reranker-v2-m3 and its int8 build, jina-reranker v1 tiny and turbo, and v2-base-multilingual. On the Qwen card's MTEB-Code run, bge-reranker-v2-m3 scores 41.38 and jina v2 58.98, against a first stage at 75.41. In octocode's matrix, bge-reranker-base cuts Hit@5 from 0.732 to 0.598. add_custom_model (README:193-205) can load other ONNX cross-encoders. However, no fastembed export of the code-capable Qwen3-Reranker-4B was found, and even with one there would still be no endpoint. Round-1 runtime candidates (llama.cpp, TEI) already cover a macOS rerank service.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: This would be overturned if fastembed, or an MCP that embeds it, served a code-capable reranker that improves Recall@5 in MTEB 2.22.5 two-stage evaluation on MTEB(code, v1) at acceptable CPU latency on the M5 Pro hosts. It would also be overturned if SocratiCode added a fastembed or ColBERT rerank stage.

claude_discover.notes:
BUDGET: gh_api is 41, one call over the 40 budget, because the MTEB latest-release lookup took two calls. The 8 web fetches were 3 Hugging Face API trending listings, the EmbeddingGemma 2, CLM-v0.1-8B and Qwen3-Reranker-4B card READMEs, octocode's RESULTS.md and the arXiv 2605.04615 abstract. They were fetched with Python urllib inside ctx_execute rather than ctx_fetch_and_index; the quotes come from the saved raw text.

REPOSITORY FORM: two proposals use huggingface.co model-repository URLs (Qwen/Qwen3-Reranker-4B and google/embeddinggemma-2), because the GitHub form does not apply to model weights. The precedent is order-2/embedding-model.json, which already uses https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Nemotron-3-Embed-1B-BF16 as the repository. Their GitHub locators (QwenLM/Qwen3-Embedding, google-deepmind/gemma) are in evidence with maintenance unknown.

VENDOR-OFFICIAL BASELINE: no native local semantic-retrieval or rerank surface was found in codex-cli 0.160.1 --help (only --search, for live web search) or in the Claude Code changelog through 2.1.292 (~/.claude/cache/changelog.md has no rerank, 'semantic search' or embedding entries). The Qdrant org pass found fastembed (assessed, not adopted) and qdrant/skills (search-quality skills, not assessed). Qdrant's OSS multistage ColBERT rerank would need SocratiCode to write multivectors.

WINNER HEALTH: none of the winners was archived, renamed or relicensed.
- SocratiCode v1.16.0 (2026-09-28) adds an opt-in Git-triggered index refresh, which is relevant to the freshness gap. HEAD is 1e829bf7ddf1 (2026-10-02). The stack installs 1.15.0 and the sealed verdict pins 1.14.0. It has no rerank stage or hook.
- vLLM v0.31.0 (2026-10-05) keeps /score and the Cohere-compatible /rerank, and still lists both reranker finalists plus Qwen3-Reranker. It adds reranker tokenization with document limits (#57666). The stack pin is 0.30.0 and the accepted pin is 0.25.0.
- Qdrant v1.19.2 comes from the layer input and was not re-fetched.

INCUMBENCY:
- SocratiCode's standing rests on native_proven compatibility, not measured quality (GAP0). The 2026-09-26 GPT-6 vote already said its uncontested status reflects incomplete coverage.
- The reranker slot's finalists rest on general-domain evidence (a BEIR average and a Recall@5 gain) with no code evidence. Their smaller alternative, bge-reranker-v2-m3, is contraindicated for code: 41.38 on MTEB-Code against a 75.41 first stage, on the Qwen card.
- The installed QMD (tobi/qmd README, default branch, lines 582-587 and 756-761) ships fixed GGUF models, embeddinggemma-300M and qwen3-reranker-0.6b-q8_0, for docs. That makes it an unselected incumbent in the embedding and reranker slots. Its 0.6B reranker is the size that regressed on MTEB-Code (73.42 against 75.41).
- The order-2 reranker packet never disposed of the Qwen3-Reranker seed.

MODEL CURRENCY: Hugging Face trending pass, created on or after 2026-09-08, without one call per vendor org because of the budget.
- Contrastive-LM/CLM-v0.1-8B (2026-09-21, Apache-2.0) is the top trending text-ranking model. Its card describes an agent state-action verifier on a frozen Qwen3-8B, encoder-locked (line 113), not a retrieval reranker. Not proposed.
- KURE and RenderRank (nlpai-lab) are Korean or visual models. Not relevant.
- perplexity-ai/pplx-embed-v2-context-9b-preview: verified only its creation date (2026-09-25), MIT license and preview status. The critic's 8.4B parameter count is unverified. No code evidence was checked. Not proposed.
- topk-io/topk-embed-v1-xsmall and -small (2026-09-23) and facebook/meta-encoder (2026-09-30) were not assessed.
- vllm-sr/Decision-2.0-* are routing classifiers.
- amazon/poiss-bge-m3-reranker (critic lead) was not verified. The critic says its base is bge-reranker-v2-m3, the generic class that regressed on code.
- Qwen3-VL-Reranker-2B/8B (2026-01-07): code scores were not verified.

CHECKED, NOT PROPOSED:
- BeaconBay/ck: no rerank in the README at HEAD. Apache-2.0, 1737 stars, pushed 2026-09-30.
- probelabs/probe: BM25 and TF-IDF with an optional BERT rerank (README:143,266), but no embedding index, so it does not fit 'compatible embedding service'.
- StarTrail-org/LEANN: only DiskANN PQ reranking (README:1287).
- kapillamba4/code-memory: BM25 plus dense search, no rerank (README:40-42).
- tobi/qmd: reranks markdown and its collection pattern is configurable (README:239), but it is markdown-first. It is a possible zero-install control arm.
- semantic-code-mcp, rag-mcp, ken, sifs and QEX: web-search hits only, unverified.
- CoREB (arXiv 2605.04615) says its data and model are released, but no repository link was found on the abstract page. It is not linked to any repository here.

HARNESS: MTEB 2.22.5 (2026-10-05) mteb/abstasks/retrieval.py supports CrossEncoderProtocol over top_ranked lists. Two-stage rerank evaluation therefore needs no self-written runner. CoIR was skipped, as directed.

SEEDS: the vendor-official pass is done. embeddinggemma-2 is proposed. No already-judged repository was re-proposed. FlagOpen/FlagEmbedding and NVIDIA/NeMo-Retriever stay as the slot finalists' sources.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: The winner stack has no qualified macOS reranking path. output.notes:
North-star action: improve source-grounded conceptual retrieval over the historical-simulation stack and broker-adapter code before independently qualified paper trading. No installation, candidate execution, benchmark or deployment occurred.

Pipeline conclusion: an upstream integration point exists, so custom glue is not justified by this sweep. ChunkHound v6.0.0 explicitly supports separate local embedding and reranker endpoints; Vera v1.4.2 supplies an optional generic reranking hook. The accepted [vLLM v0.25.0 scoring interface](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.25.0/docs/models/pooling_models/scoring.md) already lists /score, /rerank, /v1/rerank and /v2/rerank, plus both finalist checkpoints. No rerank configuration was found in the reviewed [SocratiCode README](https://github.com/giancarloerra/SocratiCode/blob/1e829bf7ddf1/README.md) or [v1.16.0 release](https://github.com/giancarloerra/SocratiCode/releases/tag/v1.16.0); installed-client inspection was unavailable, so this is a bounded documentation finding, not a universal absence claim.

Model-slot refresh, recorded here because no corresponding canonical GitHub model repository was independently established for these HF-only leads: (1) google/embeddinggemma-2 is the strongest embedding-model trial lead. Its [official card](https://huggingface.co/google/embeddinggemma-2) reports MTEB Code v1 nDCG@10 of 78.68 versus 68.76 for its predecessor, selectable encoders and 768-dimensional output. These are upstream measurements, not target-project results. The card describes approximately 740M total parameters and a 270M text component; the lead's exact 744M figure was not independently verified. Freeze checkpoint 914f7f89142e33e77833254d9c9b90c3cef7303b, correct query/document prefixes and a separate index for the comparison. [Google's supported inference guide](https://ai.google.dev/gemma/docs/embeddinggemma/multimodal-embeddinggemma-with-sentence-transformers) supplies a local CPU/GPU path; compatibility with the installed embedding service remains unverified. (2) perplexity-ai/pplx-embed-v2-context-9b-preview is keep_but_compare: its [card](https://huggingface.co/perplexity-ai/pplx-embed-v2-context-9b-preview) requires document chunks encoded together, a distinct encode_queries method, custom model code and isolated preview embeddings. These semantics are not a demonstrated drop-in fit for the current consumer. Its [weight tree](https://huggingface.co/perplexity-ai/pplx-embed-v2-context-9b-preview/tree/main) contains weights; storage size does not establish runtime VRAM consumption. (3) amazon/poiss-bge-m3-reranker is not_adopted for this requirement: the [official card](https://huggingface.co/amazon/poiss-bge-m3-reranker) describes geographic point-of-interest ranking with distance/quality fields and 256-token pairs. Its POISS improvement establishes no code-retrieval advantage. This is a domain-fit judgment, not a maintenance or license exclusion. (4) jinaai/jina-reranker-v3.5 is keep_but_compare: the [card](https://huggingface.co/jinaai/jina-reranker-v3.5) documents local Transformers inference and official MLX/GGUF variants for a 0.6B listwise model, correcting any inference that the separate MLX-only reference application makes the weights Linux-incompatible. Its CC-BY-NC-4.0 license is information only. Qualify the listwise consumer contract before comparing it: independently scored batches must not silently change the candidate-list semantics. None of these model judgments establishes target-host superiority.

Existing model controls: retain nvidia/llama-nemotron-rerank-1b-v2 and BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-gemma, with BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3 as the smaller comparator. The [recorded reranker slot](https://github.com/seathatflowsinourveins/native-agent-stack/blob/main/evidence/artifacts/new-wsl-final-architecture-20261002/added-slots/order-2/reranker-model.json) identifies finalists, not an overall measured winner. Their vLLM compatibility was independently checked; the slot's benchmark numbers were not relayed as independently reverified facts. [QMD at the supplied pin](https://github.com/tobi/qmd/blob/93d211f9ef4a/README.md) already exposes rerank=true/false and model slots, with a Qwen3-0.6B reranker default. Keep it as the document control; that does not establish code-consumer quality. Voyage rerank-3/rerank-3-lite were not proposed: the brief identifies an API-only route, and this lane did not independently inspect their files or establish a need for a new paid service.

Deciding experiment: use [MTEB 2.22.5](https://github.com/embeddings-benchmark/mteb/releases/tag/2.22.5) as the upstream harness, plus its supported custom-task mechanism for frozen target-project questions and expected source spans. First hold corpus, chunking, embedding model and top-50 candidate lists fixed to isolate reranking; compare consumer engines separately. Measure paired nDCG@5/10, Recall@5, exact-identifier regressions, p50/p95 latency and total resident/peak memory with other models present. Select a reranker only when the quality improvement is distinguishable from zero, Recall@5 does not regress, and preregistered latency/headroom limits pass on each destination host. Verify actual reranker calls, failure handling and source-span preservation. Exercise add/rename/delete, watcher kill/restart and independent-host restoration using upstream test paths. New checkpoints need revision-pinned caches and compatible index metadata; changing models must not mix embedding spaces.

Winner health: GitHub metadata still reports [SocratiCode](https://api.github.com/repos/giancarloerra/SocratiCode) unarchived/AGPL-3.0, [Qdrant](https://api.github.com/repos/qdrant/qdrant) unarchived/Apache-2.0 and [vLLM](https://api.github.com/repos/vllm-project/vllm) unarchived/Apache-2.0, with unchanged canonical ownership. [vLLM v0.31.0](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/releases/tag/v0.31.0), released 2026-10-05, is verified current; it is not thereby qualified on this WSL host. The supplied current install pins differ from the sealed winner pins. Native compatibility evidence does not establish retrieval superiority. The supplied held-out/watcher follow-up receipts were not read here, so neither 'no benchmark exists' nor gap closure is asserted. Winner quality standing remains provisional.
